1	# marvin — Working Journal
2	
3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for marvin. Newest entries at the top. For *what marvin is* (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones), read [`spec.md`](spec.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.

6	
7	**2026-07-01 — Dashboard redesign: dedicated SELECT SONG button; top-bar tap retired.** MGS regenerated the Marvin screen with a reworked dashboard: the old `PANEL_BASE_TOP`/`PANEL_BASE_BOTTOM`/`PANEL_SYSTEM_*`/`PANEL_ROBOT_CONTROLS` are gone, replaced by `PANEL_DASHBOARD_TOP`/`_BOTTOM` (+ `_TOP_LEFT`/`_TOP_RIGHT`), and the guitar strum buttons were dropped. Three code effects: (1) **Song select** now opens from a real `BUTTON_DASHBOARD_GAMEPLAY_SELECT_SONG` button (released-callback → `UiManager_OpenSongSelect`), replacing the old header-panel vtable-tap hack in `screen_dashboard.c`. (2) `screen_video.c`'s fullscreen input-gate retargeted from `BASE_TOP/BASE_BOTTOM` to `DASHBOARD_TOP/DASHBOARD_BOTTOM`. (3) This regen dropped **all** MGS auto-event wiring, so the hamburger (renamed `BUTTON_NAV_HAMBURGER`, now under `DASHBOARD_TOP_LEFT`) is wired explicitly in `ScreenNavigation_Setup` via `setPressedEventCallback`; the orphaned `event_Marvin_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION_OnPressed` was removed. The guitar strum glue in `manual_input.c` is kept as-is (orphaned but preserved) — the `ManualControl` actuator logic stays even though the UI no longer drives it, so the strum buttons can be reattached later. **Pending hardware test / build.**
8	
9	**2026-07-01 — HEO video levels expansion (gamma CLUT).** The captured source is mildly range-compressed vs the panel's full 0..255 — corpus measurement (active area, borders excluded): black cluster ~5 (dead border pedestal ~13, cropped out), white ceiling ~233, nothing ≥235. The HEO CBHS limited-range black-level block is **YCbCr-only** (datasheet §6.2.6.7 / SAM9X7 DS), so it can't touch our RGB888 HEO input; instead we use the HEO **per-component gamma CLUT** (works on true RGB, `HEOCFG1.GAM`), loaded once with a linear levels-expansion curve (`out = clamp((in−5)·255/228)`, `VIDEO_LEVELS_BLACK=5`, `WHITE=233`). Display-only — the DDR capture is untouched so the detector/gameplay see raw pixels — and free at scanout. Loaded in `UiManager_Initialize` while GAM/CLUTEN are clear (required to write `LCDC_HEOCLUT[256]`); `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode` rewrites `HEOCFG1` with `GAM(0)` on every bind, so `heo_bind` re-asserts `GAM` after it. Fixed curve (no runtime knob for the *values*), but a **`gamma <on|off>` console command** toggles the whole expansion on/off (`UiManager_SetVideoLevels`, gates `GAM` in `heo_bind` + requests a rebind) for A/B eyeballing on the panel. **Code-complete, pending hardware test** — the ~5/233 pedestal/ceiling may differ per Wii/converter, retune `VIDEO_LEVELS_*` if needed. Earlier "blacks already at 0" was wrong — conflated the rare true-0 outliers with the ~5 cluster; corrected here.
10	
11	**2026-07-01 — Rounded AA frame around the windowed video + nav→OVR2.** The windowed video (HEO, a hard rectangle) now gets a 1px rounded frame with anti-aliased corners, matching the dashboard panels (`0x404040` = `SCHEME_PANEL` `LE_SCHM_SHADOWDARK`, radius 6). Since the video is on HEO (not a canvas), the `PanelAA` backdrop-blend trick can't reach it — the frame is a **direct-driven ARGB_4444 overlay on OVR1, above HEO**, carrying true per-pixel alpha so the LCDC composites it over the video. Z-order is `OVR2>OVR1>HEO>BASE` (`VIDPRI(0)`), and the open nav drawer covers the video's left edge, so the frame must sit *below* nav → **nav moved OVR1→OVR2**, frame took OVR1. The GFX canvas framework has no 4444 mode (`gfxColorMode` only 5551/8888), so the overlay is driven directly via the XLCDC PLIB (splash/HEO-style), buffer filled once from a rounded-rect SDF: corner-cut opaque black (dashboard backdrop), 1px stroke, transparent interior; alpha AA on the stroke→video edge. New `ui_manager` verbs: `UiManager_VideoOverlayShow/Hide` (OVR1) and `UiManager_ShowNavLayer/HideNavLayer` (nav on OVR2 via `bind_canvas`, which pokes RGB565 each open since album-art leaves OVR2 in RGBA8888). Reveal-time OVR1 RGB565 poke dropped (OVR1 users now self-poke). Frame lifecycle = "windowed video visible": shown by `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed`, hidden on fullscreen enter and song-select open. Layer map now: BASE=dash, HEO=video, OVR1=video-frame/song-select-dialog, OVR2=nav/album-art (frame⇎dialog and nav⇎album-art are time-exclusive; frame hidden whenever video is). Design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md) §16. **Code-complete, pending hardware test.** Watch for CSI-2 capture stalls — the overlay adds an always-on ~41 MB/s OVR1 read while windowed. **Future:** this OVR1 overlay is also where a **per-frame gameplay HUD** (note-highway markers, hit/miss, detected-note boxes) would be drawn over the video — direct buffer raster, no Legato (canvas framework can't own it and per-frame Legato repaint is too heavy), must be fast/minimal-overhead (incremental redraw), and double-buffered with a vsync address flip to avoid tearing. HUD coords map to the *displayed* window, so source-derived positions apply the §15 active-area crop+scale. See `ui_compositor.md` §16.1.
12	
13	**2026-07-01 — Runtime active-picture detection + HEO source-crop.** The component→HDMI (Wii) source frames its active raster with dead black bars whose thickness varies by console/converter, so the active area is **detected at runtime**, not hardcoded. Offline analysis of the 101-frame `docs/gh3_screens` corpus (720×480 captures): active area ≈ **716×448 @ (0,15)** (top 15 / bottom 17 / right 4 / left 0), and — key finding — the bars are **not** black=0; they sit at a ~13 pedestal, the *same* level as in-video black (so a `>0` test can't separate them). What separates cleanly is brightness: border max ≤ ~14, content ≥ ~145, so a **fixed luma threshold (max of B,G,R > 40)** splits them with wide margin and no pedestal dependence (validated: recovers the exact box on 99/101 frames, all 101 pass a ≥700×420 gate). Bonus: 716×448 = 1.598 ≈ the panel's 1.600, so cropping to the active area makes fullscreen essentially aspect-correct. Implementation: `video.c` detector (`Video_GetActiveRect`) scans inward from each edge (bounded to the deepest border the min-size gate allows, so a dark loading frame is cheap), unions the bright bounds over 16 *bright* frames (dark frames find no content and are skipped), then locks if ≥700×420 — one-shot per capture arm, reset on re-arm/source-size change, full-frame fallback until locked. The compositor (`ui_manager` `heo_bind`) consumes the rect as the **HEO source crop**: offset the frame base by `y*stride + x*bpp`, size `HEOCFG4` to the active w/h, skip cropped columns via `XSTRIDE = (src_w-active_w)*bpp` (matches the GFX driver's own `FB_TYPE_SZ*(resx-sizex)`); `heo_frame_latch` adds the same offset per ring slot; `heo_reconcile` rebinds when the rect changes (detection flipping full→cropped). Applies to both windowed and fullscreen. **Code-complete, pending hardware test.**
14	
15	**2026-07-01 — Tap-to-fullscreen live video (`screen_video`).** Tap the live video on the dashboard to blow it up to fullscreen (HEO stretch-to-fill across 1280×800); tap anywhere to shrink back to the windowed 720×480 rect. New `screens/video/screen_video.{c,h}` module — a screen module *without a canvas* (the video is on the HEO hardware layer, compositor-owned), so it owns only the interaction: a `touchDownEvent` re-pointed onto `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD` (the full-screen layer-0 catch-all under the IGNOREPICK `root0`). Relies on Legato's touch **bubbling** (`legato_input.c` walks `targetWidget->parent` until a widget calls `leWidgetEvent_Accept`) — plain panels never accept, so a video-region tap bubbles up to the dashboard panel; windowed→tap-in-rect enters fullscreen via `UiManager_VideoShow(0,0,BASE_W,BASE_H)`. To exit from anywhere, fullscreen gates picking off on `Marvin_PANEL_BASE_TOP` + `Marvin_PANEL_BASE_BOTTOM` (the two subtrees holding every interactive dashboard widget) by clearing `LE_WIDGET_ENABLED` (flag-only, no repaint — same gate as `ui_manager`'s `panel_set_pickable`), so every tap then resolves to the dashboard panel and exits. Windowed placement is now owned by `SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_*` in `screen_video.h` (moved out of `ui_manager`'s `VIDEO_WIN_*`); `ui_manager` calls `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed()` at reveal and on song-select close. `base_discard_reconcile` follows the video rect, so fullscreen discards BASE DMA across the whole panel (free bandwidth win). Design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md) §14. **Pending hardware test.** (The windowed HEO rect (280,76) lines up with the `VIDEO_STREAM` placeholder panel — abs (280,77) once its `BASE_BOTTOM`→`BASE_CENTER` parent offsets are summed. Fullscreen can't be entered with the nav drawer open: nav is modal (`UiManager_SetDashboardPickable(false)`), so the dashboard — and the video tap — is un-pickable while it's open.)

17	**UI architecture — nav drawer complete; song/mode-select dialog is the next UI step.** The canvas compositor + per-screen-module model is built and validated on hardware: `ui_manager` orchestrates screens (string table + `screenInit/Show`; the MGS screen state machine is disabled, worked around with the `compat/le_gen_init.h` stub), the dashboard is its own MGS Screen on BASE, and the nav drawer is its own MGS Screen (`Navigation`) re-hosted onto OVR1 — they coexist live (no active-screen gate; `leUpdate`/`leInput` cover all attached layers). `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=3 is pinned via the never-shown `LayerBudget` screen. **Nav drawer is feature-complete:** slides in/out via canvas Move FX (`NAV_CLOSED_X` dodges the window-clip row-wrap; mid-slide reversal cancels the in-flight move), single-active highlight (Dashboard closes, others switch), clean close, rounded buttons with anti-aliased corners (`ui/widgets/button_aa/widget_button_aa.c`, per-instance vtable re-point — see `ui_compositor.md` §10a). Authoritative design + the window-clip/alignment gotchas in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md); decisions 2026-06-25. **Next (decided 2026-06-29): migrate to MGS's single-master-screen / layer-screen model** — one master Legato screen named `Marvin` with one layer per panel (dashboard, nav, song-select, dialogs…), replacing the current "separate 1-layer MGS Screen per panel, manually re-hosted, `LE_LAYER_COUNT` pinned by the fake `LayerBudget` screen" approach. MGS then derives `LE_LAYER_COUNT` and auto-associates each layer-screen with its canvas, so the `LayerBudget` hack, the `compat/le_gen_init.h` stub, and the disconnect/re-host dance all go away; `ui_manager` shrinks to buffer assignment + `show_layer`/`hide_layer` verbs. **Splash stays separate/manual** (pre-Legato RGBA8888) on a canvas slot outside the layer-screen range. Authoritative model + direction now in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md) §0. SongSelect (MGS screen already generated, committed `1e16ac9`) becomes a Marvin layer-screen rather than a standalone Screen. The earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable / reveal-then-promote" framing is **superseded** (a state-machine artifact).

19	**Song-select operator UI — scrollable list widget built & validated on hardware.** Custom Legato widget `ui/song_list.{h,c}` (a hand-written `leWidget` subclass) renders the SELECT SONG setlist (tier badge + bold title + dim artist + right-aligned duration), driven by a decoupled row-provider callback (no catalog dependency); drag-scroll with time-based kinetic inertia, tap-to-select. Bring-up via the `songlist` console command + a catalog-backed demo provider (`ui/song_list_demo.{c,h}`) — scroll/select/opaque-fill confirmed on hardware. **Bringing it up surfaced and fixed a real Legato/GFX2D cache-coherency bug** (see decision log 2026-06-24): the CPU-rendered scratch buffer was cacheable, so the 2D-engine blit leaked stale pixels through opaque widgets — fixed by placing the scratch in non-cached DDR. **Next:** author the full SELECT SONG screen in MGS (album art + catalog-fed metadata panel + difficulty/mode/Select), and the **tier / career-setlist data model** (the `tier` badge needs the deferred catalog tier column). Two upstream Microchip Legato/gfx bugs to file (decision log).

21	**Song catalog loader — built and committed; exercised on hardware via the `catalog`/`songlist` console commands.** New `game/catalog.{h,c}` maps the recognizer's `(setlist, index)` → human labels (title/artist/bpm/length) from `<card>/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv`, so the UI/high-score display shows names instead of `#4`. Flat **CSV** (decided over the spec's JSON for the same reasons `results` is CSV — no on-device tokenizer, `FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1`, static buffers, pandas/Excel-editable). The two CSV helpers were extracted out of `results.c` into a shared `util/csv.{h,c}` and the catalog reuses them. Lazy-loads once into a fixed `[GP_N_SONGS]` static cache (file closed after load), so lookups are O(n) in RAM and don't fight `results.csv` for the single FatFs handle. `catalog` console command (`reload` / `ls` / `<main|bonus> <index>`) validates the path against a checked-in seed catalog (`data/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv`). Columns: `setlist,index,title,artist,album,bpm,length_s,year,genre,difficulty`. `title`/`artist`/`album` are real, sourced from the `SONGS` table in `tools/fetch_gh3_cover_art.py` (incl. proper UTF-8 — *Héroes del Silencio*, *Mauvais Garçon*); that script gained a `--catalog` mode that also fills `year`/`genre` from MusicBrainz on a networked run. `bpm`/`length_s`/`difficulty` are reserved-but-blank (GH3 surfaces no per-song difficulty; the authentic signal is the career tier, deferred). Catalog is labels only: a missing/stale card degrades to "Unknown song" and never touches recognition (compile-time in flash). **Deferred:** the stale-catalog version warning — `export_c.py` doesn't emit `GP_METADATA_VERSION` yet (open item below). **Next SD consumer:** album-artwork pre-cache (spec §4.8.7) — directory structure is now locked (`art/{small,large}/<setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}`, one size-tier subdir per DDR cache). **Built 2026-06-30** (`game/art.{c,h}`, decision log): all covers decoded once into static RGB888 DDR caches during the splash, `(setlist,index)`→`leImage*` lookup, song-select strip wired; large tier is a 508×208 strip with a difficulty-colored fade baked offline. Dashboard small-thumbnail consumer still pending (no MGS slot yet).

23	**T1S inter-node link — built and working (marvin ↔ guitar).** marvin is the PLCA **coordinator** (node 0) on a 10BASE-T1S bus (LAN8651 over FLEXCOM4 SPI); hand-authored stack in `default/src/net/t1s/`. It sends the actuator command over T1S to the `guitar` follower node (id 2), which actuates the Wii GPIOs (guitar G1+G2 proven). Followers announce presence via a heartbeat (ethertype `0x88B6`); the `t1s` and `nodes` console commands report link/credits/per-node presence. Transport is behind `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT={UART,T1S}` (T1S default on the `t1s` branch). The `fretboard` node (id 1) firmware is now **written, T1S-only** (fretboard journal 2026-06-17): it streams its 17-byte frame to marvin **and** drives the `guitar` node directly — its on-device model infers the bitmask and sends it peer-to-peer to `02:..:02`. marvin's RX side needed no changes — `fretboard_link.c`'s T1S frame handler already parses the frame from node id 1 (`DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD`) and the node-table + heartbeat-presence demux already cover it. **Next (marvin side):** **active-source arbitration** — both marvin (timing pipeline) and the fretboard now address the guitar (`02:..:02`), so marvin needs active-detector/active-guitar selection to ensure exactly one source drives at a time (the fretboard's SW0 is an interim manual arm; until then, don't run marvin's timing pipeline to the guitar while the fretboard is armed). Then fretboard hardware bring-up. PoDL is design-direction only. Detail in [`../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md); decision log entry 2026-06-17.

TC358743 control) also moved off FLEXCOM6/PA24-PA25 to FLEXCOM8 TWI/PB4-PB5 during the port — `spec.md` §3.1/§3.2 reconciled on 2026-06-08. Next: pick the v0 algorithm (Q8) and start populating `fret[]`.

42	## Decision log
43	
44	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
45	|------|----------|-----------|
46	| 2026-07-01 | **UI: paint every screen canvas once at boot; show/hide is repaint-free. Fixes the ~0.5–1 s first-touch lag after opening/closing the nav drawer or song-select modal.** Root cause: Legato defers all touch input while its renderer is non-idle (`handleTouchDown`/up/move return `LE_EVENT_DEFERRED` when `leIsDrawing()`, `legato_input.c`), re-queuing the event every 10 ms `LEGATO_Tasks` tick. A screen transition kicked off a full repaint that held the renderer busy for many ticks, stranding the first tap behind it. The repaints were architecturally needless — each screen owns a RAM canvas surface and Legato renders into it regardless of the canvas's shown/bound state (`GFX_IOCTL_SET_ACTIVE_LAYER` succeeds for any canvas), so showing a screen should be a pure HW-layer bind. Three offenders removed: (1) `navigation_open()` explicit `PANEL_NAVIGATION->invalidate()` every open; (2) `songsel_set_input()` used `setEnabled()` for modal input-gating, and `_leWidget_SetEnabled` invalidates on state change → repainted the modal panels on open and the **dashboard** on close; (3) same `setEnabled(DASHBOARD)` in nav open/close. **Fix:** `panel_set_pickable()` in `ui_manager.c` toggles `LE_WIDGET_ENABLED` directly on `wgt->flags` (no invalidate — the renderer never reads ENABLED; `leUtils_PickFromWidget` descends only into ENABLED children, so clearing it gates the whole subtree). `UiManager_SetDashboardPickable(bool)` shares one dashboard gate between nav + song-select. New `paint_all_screens_once()` invalidates all four panels (dashboard/nav/song-select/album-art) behind the splash before `wait_render_idle()`, so every surface is complete before first show. Removed the now-redundant one-time invalidate in `ScreenSongSelect_Setup`. Content-change repaints (album-art swap on song tap, nav highlight scheme) are unchanged. Real reason the old startup paint "didn't fully land": MGS builds `PANEL_NAVIGATION` `setVisible(FALSE)`, so the boot root-damage painted nothing until `Setup` flipped it — the explicit boot paint makes it deterministic. Builds clean (XC32 v5.10); **pending on-hardware confirm** that first-tap lag is gone on nav open/close + song-select open/tap/close. `IGNOREPICK` was rejected for the gate: it stops a panel being the pick result but still lets its children be picked, so it wouldn't gate the subtree. The heavy 508×208 RGBA8888 album-art alpha blit remains a separate perf item. | Legato's input-while-drawing deferral is library behavior (can't edit vendor tree); the lever is to make transitions not repaint at all, which the canvas model already affords. Confirmed the enabling fact in code: Legato's only "where do I render" knob is the active layer's `pixelBuffer.pixels` (it paints a scratch buffer, then `DRV_XLCDC_BlitBuffer` copies into `drvLayer[activeLayer].pixelBuffer`); there is **no** stock Legato API to render a widget tree into an arbitrary off-screen buffer. **GFX Canvas is exactly that missing indirection** — `GFXC_GetPixelBuffer` hands Legato a canvas object's buffer and `gfxcSetBaseCanvasID` switches which canvas a layer renders into, with `gfxcSetLayer`/show/hide/position/alpha + fade/move on top. Layer budget: `BASE`=background, `OVR1`/`OVR2`=swappable overlays (to be enabled — `XLCDC_TOT_LAYERS` is 2 today), `HEO`=live camera (off-limits). Legato stays the **renderer** (fonts, `song_list`); a thin `ui/` compositor owns surface↔layer multiplexing. Touch handled by **reveal-then-promote** (parked surfaces are non-interactive; promote to a live Legato layer to interact). Phased plan P0–P5 + open questions in the doc. **Design only — no code/MCC yet.** | Reverses the earlier "back off canvas" — that call was made on the **wrong axis**: canvas was dismissed for the *slide animation* (which direct `XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos` stepping handles fine, no framework needed), but the actual problem is the **off-screen surface pool** (render content decoupled from a hardware layer), and that is canvas's literal reason to exist. The two homegrown alternatives lose: DIY pixel-buffer retarget reimplements canvas's per-surface/scratch/binding bookkeeping (~half of canvas, growing once surfaces aren't full-screen); direct-layer-only can present/animate but can't get Legato content *into* a surface. Canvas's earlier objections are addressable, not fatal: it deletes the static `frame_buffer` array, but we *use* the canvas buffers as our surfaces (statically allocated, non-cached per the 2026-06-24 fix), so static-allocation holds; the dynamic `GFX_CANVAS_Task` converts to `xTaskCreateStatic` or rides alongside the existing MCC dynamic tasks. Binding constraint is **layers (2 free), not memory** (~21 MB free in the 32 MB `ram_nocache` after the ISC pool + scratch; full-screen RGB565 ≈ 2 MB, most overlays far less). Resolves spec Q5 for the *presentation* layer (Legato renderer + canvas compositor) without dictating per-screen authoring. |
59	| 2026-06-24 | **Legato CPU-render scratch buffer must live in non-cached DDR (`.region_nocache`) — fixed a GFX2D cache-coherency bleed; grew `ram_nocache` 16→32 MB.** Symptom (found during song-list bring-up): dashboard content streakily "bled through" an opaque overlay widget, intermittently, only where CPU-rendered text was. Active render path is **CPU software** (`leRenderer_FillArea` → `_RGBBlendFill`; glyphs too) into a **scratch buffer**, then **`DRV_GFX2D_Blit`** (the SAM9X75 2D engine) copies scratch→framebuffer. The framebuffer is non-cached (`FB_CACHE_NC` → `.region_nocache`) but the Legato scratch was **cacheable**: `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` was an empty no-op `#define` and `LE_COHERENT_ATTR = CACHE_ALIGN` (alignment only). The blit's `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` of the cached scratch is insufficient on ARM926 → the 2D engine reads stale CPU-cached lines → streaky, cache-line-granularity bleed. **Fix:** define `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR = __attribute__((section(".region_nocache")))` in **`user.cmake`** (the `#ifndef` guard in the generated `legato_renderer.c` lets the `-D` win → survives MGS regen, no generated-tree patch); MCC grew `ram_nocache` 16→32 MB to host it (ddram.ld + plib_mmu.c + `DDRAM_NO_CACHE_SIZE`). **Confirmed on hardware** (commits `d36640f` + `c0f316c`). **Two upstream Microchip Legato/gfx bugs to file:** (1) with "Cacheable Frame Buffers" **off**, the generator non-caches the framebuffer but leaves the Legato render scratch cacheable (`LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` empty) — the gap that bit us; (2) `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` omits the `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` that `DRV_GFX2D_Blit` has (latent — bites any GPU-fill config, e.g. `LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE=1`). | Root-caused by elimination, not by reading (every software-logic path traced correct): a bare opaque magenta fill still bled, hiding the dashboard cleared it, and non-cached scratch fixed it → it's the cached-scratch ↔ 2D-engine coherency, below the software layer. Non-cached is the correct policy on this SoC — Microchip already chose it for the framebuffer (`FB_CACHE_NC`) rather than trusting cache maintenance for a DMA-/GPU-read buffer; the scratch is the same kind of buffer and should match. Adding cache maintenance to `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` would *not* fix this (Fill isn't on the path; the on-path `Blit` already invalidates and still leaked). System-wide rule for this board: any buffer the 2D engine or display DMA reads must be non-cached (or carry correct, sufficient maintenance — which the cacheable path here does not). |
60	| 2026-06-24 | **Song-select setlist = a hand-written custom Legato widget (`leWidget` subclass), not the stock list widget.** `ui/song_list.{h,c}`: subclass with overridden `_paint`/`update`/touch handlers. Stock `leListWidget` is disabled **and** its item model (icon + one string) can't render the tier-badge + two-line + right-aligned-duration row. Design: **row-provider callback** `songlist_row_fn` (widget never includes `game/catalog.h`; the screen owns catalog→row mapping + future tier grouping); **drag + kinetic inertia** computed from the **FreeRTOS tick** (`leUpdate(0)` means the framework `dt` is always 0, so the widget measures real elapsed time itself for frame-rate-independent motion); **tap-to-select** (<10 px movement) with a selection callback; **virtualized software paint** (`leRenderer_RectFill` + `leStringRenderer_DrawCString`, visible rows only, no per-row child widgets); single **pool allocation** with the vtable built by **copying the base vtable at runtime** (project builds `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES=0`, so `_leWidget_FillVTable` isn't linkable and the GenerateVTable path is compiled out); declared **opaque** (`BACKGROUND_FILL`) so Legato composites it. Lives entirely in `ui/` (added via `user.cmake`) — zero edits to the generated `gfx/legato/` tree. Bring-up: `ui/song_list_demo.{c,h}` + a `songlist` console command (`attach`/`off`/`hide`/`show`/`solid`/`tree`/`stats`) with a catalog-backed provider; **validated on hardware**. | Matches the project's MCC-isolation idiom (own module + `user.cmake`, like `console`/`perf_log`); the widget is the primary, reusable piece, so it was built first, ahead of the MGS screen around it. Row-provider keeps the widget generic and testable and lets the screen map `Catalog_At(i)` → row (and supply tier badges once the tier column exists). Pool allocation (not static) because Legato recursively `LE_FREE`s the whole child tree on screen teardown (`legato_widget.c`) — a static widget attached to a screen would feed a static pointer to `LE_FREE`; the Legato widget pool is the accepted heap carve-out, and the widget is one self-contained allocation (fixed internal scratch, no secondary mallocs). Time-based inertia (vs per-tick) because the update cadence is render-bound (~55 Hz) and irregular under the priority-2 UI task. Tier badges blank until the deferred catalog `tier` column lands. |

1	#include "game/gameplay_select.h"
2	#include "game/gameplay_metadata.h"
3	
4	#include <math.h>
5	#include <stddef.h>
6	#include <stdint.h>
7	
8	#define GP_BPP            3
9	#define GP_SEL_MAX_CELLS  16   /* >= max items on any modelled menu (7) */
10	
11	/* Split [0, extent) into `n` spans; edge(i) = round(i*extent/n). */
12	static int gp_edge(int i, int extent, int n)
13	{
14	    return (int)lround((double)i * (double)extent / (double)n);
15	}
16	
17	const gp_menu_layout_t *gp_menu_for_screen(uint8_t screen)
18	{
19	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_N_MENUS; i++)
20	    {
21	        if (gp_menus[i].screen == screen) { return &gp_menus[i]; }
22	    }
23	    return NULL;
24	}
25	
26	/* Mean BGR over [x0,x1)×[y0,y1), clamped to the frame. */
27	static void gp_rect_mean_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, int w, int h,
28	                             int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1, float out[3])
29	{
30	    if (x0 < 0) { x0 = 0; }  if (x1 > w) { x1 = w; }
31	    if (y0 < 0) { y0 = 0; }  if (y1 > h) { y1 = h; }
32	    uint32_t sb = 0u, sg = 0u, sr = 0u, n = 0u;
33	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
34	    {
35	        const uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)w + (uint32_t)x0) * GP_BPP;
36	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
37	        {
38	            sb += p[0]; sg += p[1]; sr += p[2];
39	            p += GP_BPP;
40	            n++;
41	        }
42	    }
43	    if (n == 0u) { out[0] = out[1] = out[2] = 0.0f; return; }
44	    out[0] = (float)sb / (float)n;
45	    out[1] = (float)sg / (float)n;
46	    out[2] = (float)sr / (float)n;
47	}
48	
49	int gp_read_selection(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height,
50	                      const gp_menu_layout_t *menu)
51	{
52	    if (width != GP_CANON_W || height != GP_CANON_H) { return -1; }
53	    int count = menu->count;
54	    if (count > GP_SEL_MAX_CELLS) { count = GP_SEL_MAX_CELLS; }
55	
56	    float col[GP_SEL_MAX_CELLS][3];
57	    int bx0 = menu->band[0], by0 = menu->band[1], bx1 = menu->band[2], by1 = menu->band[3];
58	    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)
59	    {
60	        int x0, y0, x1, y1;
61	        if (menu->axis == GP_AXIS_H)
62	        {
63	            y0 = by0; y1 = by1;
64	            x0 = bx0 + gp_edge(c, bx1 - bx0, count);
65	            x1 = bx0 + gp_edge(c + 1, bx1 - bx0, count);
66	        }
67	        else
68	        {
69	            x0 = bx0; x1 = bx1;
70	            y0 = by0 + gp_edge(c, by1 - by0, count);
71	            y1 = by0 + gp_edge(c + 1, by1 - by0, count);
72	        }
73	        gp_rect_mean_bgr(frame, width, height, x0, y0, x1, y1, col[c]);
74	    }
75	
76	    /* Normalize per frame: subtract per-channel mean across cells, divide by the
77	     * scalar spread (matches highlight.cell_colors in the prototype). */
78	    float mean[3] = {0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f};
79	    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)
80	        for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++) { mean[ch] += col[c][ch]; }
81	    for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++) { mean[ch] /= (float)count; }
82	
83	    double var = 0.0;
84	    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)
85	        for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++)
86	        {
87	            double d = (double)col[c][ch] - (double)mean[ch];
88	            var += d * d;
89	        }
90	    float std = (float)sqrt(var / (double)(count * 3));
91	    if (std < 1e-6f) { std = 1.0f; }
92	
93	    int best = 0;
94	    float best_dev = -1.0f;
95	    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)
96	    {
97	        const float *base = &menu->baseline[c * 3];
98	        float dev = 0.0f;
99	        for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++)
100	        {
101	            float v = (col[c][ch] - mean[ch]) / std;
102	            float d = v - base[ch];
103	            dev += d * d;
104	        }
105	        if (dev > best_dev) { best_dev = dev; best = c; }
106	    }
107	    return best;
108	}
109	
110	/* ── song_select ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
111	
112	/* Per-frame-normalized low-res luma grid over an ROI, offset by (dx,dy). */
113	static void gp_song_grid(const uint8_t *frame, int w, int h,
114	                         const int roi[4], int dx, int dy, float *out)
115	{
116	    int x0 = roi[0] + dx, y0 = roi[1] + dy;
117	    int pw = roi[2] - roi[0], ph = roi[3] - roi[1];
118	    for (int r = 0; r < GP_SONG_ROWS; r++)
119	    {
120	        int cy0 = y0 + gp_edge(r, ph, GP_SONG_ROWS);
121	        int cy1 = y0 + gp_edge(r + 1, ph, GP_SONG_ROWS);
122	        if (cy0 < 0) { cy0 = 0; }  if (cy1 > h) { cy1 = h; }
123	        for (int c = 0; c < GP_SONG_COLS; c++)
124	        {
125	            int cx0 = x0 + gp_edge(c, pw, GP_SONG_COLS);
126	            int cx1 = x0 + gp_edge(c + 1, pw, GP_SONG_COLS);
127	            if (cx0 < 0) { cx0 = 0; }  if (cx1 > w) { cx1 = w; }
128	            double s = 0.0; uint32_t n = 0u;
129	            for (int y = cy0; y < cy1; y++)
130	            {
131	                const uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)w + (uint32_t)cx0) * GP_BPP;
132	                for (int x = cx0; x < cx1; x++)
133	                {
134	                    s += (double)p[0] * 29.0 + (double)p[1] * 150.0 + (double)p[2] * 77.0;
135	                    p += GP_BPP;
136	                    n++;
137	                }
138	            }
139	            out[r * GP_SONG_COLS + c] = (n != 0u) ? (float)(s / 256.0 / (double)n) : 0.0f;
140	        }
141	    }
142	    double sum = 0.0;
143	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++) { sum += out[i]; }
144	    float mean = (float)(sum / (double)GP_SONG_LEN);
145	    double var = 0.0;
146	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++)
147	    {
148	        double d = (double)out[i] - (double)mean;
149	        var += d * d;
150	    }
151	    float std = (float)sqrt(var / (double)GP_SONG_LEN);
152	    if (std < 1e-6f) { std = 1.0f; }
153	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++) { out[i] = (out[i] - mean) / std; }
154	}
155	
156	/* Offset-search grids, both ROIs. Static — single observer-task caller. */
157	static float s_slot_grids[GP_SONG_NDX * GP_SONG_NDY][GP_SONG_LEN];
158	static float s_first_grids[GP_SONG_NDX * GP_SONG_NDY][GP_SONG_LEN];
159	
160	int gp_read_song(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height, gp_song_t *out)
161	{
162	    if (width != GP_CANON_W || height != GP_CANON_H)
163	    {
164	        out->setlist = 0; out->index = 0; out->tmpl = -1;
165	        return -1;
166	    }
167	    static const int slot_roi[4]  = GP_SONG_SLOT_ROI;
168	    static const int first_roi[4] = GP_SONG_FIRST_ROI;
169	
170	    int noff = 0;
171	    for (int ix = 0; ix < GP_SONG_NDX; ix++)
172	        for (int iy = 0; iy < GP_SONG_NDY; iy++)
173	        {
174	            gp_song_grid(frame, width, height, slot_roi,  gp_song_dx[ix], gp_song_dy[iy], s_slot_grids[noff]);
175	            gp_song_grid(frame, width, height, first_roi, gp_song_dx[ix], gp_song_dy[iy], s_first_grids[noff]);
176	            noff++;
177	        }
178	
179	    float best_d = 1e30f;
180	    int best_t = -1;
181	    for (int t = 0; t < GP_N_SONGS; t++)
182	    {
183	        const float *vec = gp_song_templates[t].vec;
184	        const float (*grids)[GP_SONG_LEN] =
185	            (gp_song_templates[t].roi_kind == GP_SONG_ROI_FIRST) ? s_first_grids : s_slot_grids;
186	        float tbest = 1e30f;
187	        for (int o = 0; o < noff; o++)
188	        {
189	            float d = 0.0f;
190	            for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++) { d += fabsf(grids[o][i] - vec[i]); }
191	            if (d < tbest) { tbest = d; }
192	        }
193	        if (tbest < best_d) { best_d = tbest; best_t = t; }
194	    }
195	
196	    out->tmpl = (int16_t)best_t;
197	    out->setlist = (best_t >= 0) ? gp_song_templates[best_t].setlist : 0;
198	    out->index = (best_t >= 0) ? gp_song_templates[best_t].index : 0;
199	    return 0;
200	}

9	/* Album-artwork cache: decodes every cover under
10	 * <card>/games/gh3-wii/art/{small,large}/ once at boot into static, fixed-size
11	 * RGB888 slots in DDR (spec §4.8.7). Runtime access is then an O(1) leImage*
12	 * pointer — no card I/O, no decode, no allocation at use time.
13	 *
14	 * Two size tiers, each a fixed slot dimension:
15	 *   small  144x144  (dashboard now-playing thumbnail)         JPEG on card
16	 *   large  508x208  (song-select detail strip, difficulty fade baked offline) PNG on card
17	 *
18	 * Covers are keyed by the recognizer's stable (setlist, index). A missing,
19	 * oversized, wrong-size, or corrupt file simply leaves its slot empty; the
20	 * lookup returns NULL and the UI shows a blank — the loader never fails boot. */
21	
22	void Art_Initialize(void);   /* state only; no I/O (call before scheduler) */
23	
24	/* Mount the card and decode all covers in both tiers into the caches. Idempotent
25	 * after the first successful pass. Returns the total number of covers decoded.
26	 * Must run from a task (blocks on SD I/O) and after Legato's image decoders are
27	 * up — i.e. during the boot/splash sequence. */
28	int  Art_LoadAll(void);
29	bool Art_IsLoaded(void);
30	
31	/* Decoded cover for (setlist, index), or NULL if absent/failed. The pointer is
32	 * stable for the life of the cache (no reload today). */
33	const leImage *Art_Large(uint8_t setlist, uint8_t index);
34	const leImage *Art_Small(uint8_t setlist, uint8_t index);
35	
36	int  Art_CountSmall(void);

11	/* Canvas ids — the per-layer-screen render surfaces in the GFX_CANVAS pool.
12	 *
13	 * The three Marvin layer-screens render into canvas[i] for Legato layer i (the
14	 * renderer maps Legato layer i → canvas[baseCanvasID + i], base 0), so these
15	 * canvas ids are pinned equal to their layer index — NOT free. A canvas is bound
16	 * to a *hardware* layer at display time by the compositor — that binding is
17	 * independent and runtime (see HW_* + bind_canvas). The boot splash is NOT a
18	 * canvas: it drives its hardware layer directly (see splash.h). */
19	#define CANVAS_DASH        0u   /* Marvin layer 0 — dashboard (base view)    */
20	#define CANVAS_NAVIGATION  1u   /* Marvin layer 1 — navigation drawer        */
21	#define CANVAS_SONGSEL     2u   /* Marvin layer 2 — song/mode-select dialog  */
22	#define CANVAS_ALBUM_ART   3u   /* Marvin layer 3 — song-select cover (RGB888) */
23	
24	/* LCDC hardware-layer indices (drvLayer / layerOrder): BASE 0, HEO 1, OVR1 2,
25	 * OVR2 3. HEO is the live camera (off-limits). A canvas is bound to a hardware
26	 * layer at *display time* by the compositor (ui_manager) via gfxcSetLayer — a
27	 * screen never owns a layer. The HW-layer budget limits how many canvases can be
28	 * *visible at once*, not how many screens can be built. */
29	#define HW_BASE   0u
30	#define HW_OVR1   2u
31	#define HW_OVR2   3u
32	
33	#define BASE_W   1280u
34	#define BASE_H    800u
35	
36	/* Hardware layer the boot splash is shown on. OVR1 (above BASE so it covers the
37	 * dashboard); OVR2 is left free for an overlay drawn over the splash, e.g. a
38	 * loading bar. */
39	#define SPLASH_HW_LAYER   HW_OVR1
40	
41	/* Bring up the UI. Call once from APP_Initialize, before the scheduler and after
42	 * Legato_Initialize. Assigns the per-screen canvas surfaces and creates the boot
43	 * task that runs the bring-up sequence (splash → screens → reveal) once the
44	 * scheduler is up. Pure setup; no screen is built or shown here. */
45	void UiManager_Initialize(void);
46	
47	/* Register a callback fired the instant the splash is on screen, from the boot
48	 * task. The app uses it to start everything else (services + camera) in parallel
49	 * with the behind-the-splash screen painting, so the system is warm at reveal.
50	 * Set before UiManager_Initialize. */
51	void UiManager_SetSplashShownCallback(void (*cb)(void));
52	
53	/* Video (HEO layer) display control. The compositor owns the HEO hardware layer;
54	 * video.c is the capture producer. Show binds the live capture to HEO at the given
55	 * panel rect (bilinear-scaled if the rect differs from the source), taking effect
56	 * once the source locks; Hide disables HEO output (capture keeps running). Layout
57	 * (the rect) is compositor policy. */
58	void UiManager_VideoShow(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t w, uint32_t h);
59	void UiManager_VideoHide(void);
60	
61	/* Toggle the HEO video levels-expansion (limited→full range via the gamma CLUT).
62	 * On by default. Display-only; takes effect on the next HEO (re)bind (a rebind is
63	 * requested so a shown video updates within a frame). For A/B eyeballing. */
64	void UiManager_SetVideoLevels(bool on);
65	bool UiManager_GetVideoLevels(void);
66	
67	/* Video frame overlay (OVR1, above HEO). Show binds a caller-owned ARGB_4444
68	 * framebuffer to OVR1 at the given panel rect (drawn on top of the video for the
69	 * rounded anti-aliased frame); Hide disables OVR1. The buffer must stay resident
70	 * while shown. Compositor owns the OVR1 register writes. */
71	void UiManager_VideoOverlayShow(const void *buf, uint32_t x, uint32_t y,
72	                                uint32_t w, uint32_t h);
73	void UiManager_VideoOverlayHide(void);
74	
75	/* Bind / unbind the navigation drawer's canvas to its hardware layer (OVR2, above
76	 * the video frame so the drawer covers it when open). Show sets OVR2 to the
77	 * drawer's RGB565 mode; the drawer module drives the slide. */
78	void UiManager_ShowNavLayer(void);
79	void UiManager_HideNavLayer(void);
80	
81	/* Show / hide the song-select dialog as a modal pair: the RGB565 dialog on OVR1 and
82	 * its full-color cover strip on OVR2 are bound + shown (open) or hidden together
83	 * (close). Closing frees OVR1 for the nav drawer. Both are no-ops if already in the
84	 * requested state. The dialog starts closed at boot. */
85	void UiManager_OpenSongSelect(void);
86	void UiManager_CloseSongSelect(void);
87	
88	/* Gate the dashboard's touch pickability without repainting it. Called by the
89	 * modal screens (nav drawer, song-select) to make the dashboard a true modal
90	 * backdrop while one is open: false = dashboard ignores touches, true = live.
91	 * Toggles pickability only — the dashboard surface is never re-drawn. */
92	void UiManager_SetDashboardPickable(bool on);

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**When should the dashboard SONG card update to reflect the dialog's selection?**

Options:
- **SELECT commits, X cancels** - Dashboard updates only when SELECT is pressed; the X (close) button dismisses without changing the dashboard. SELECT becomes the commit point the future gameplay engine hooks into.
- **Both SELECT and X commit** - Any dialog dismissal pushes the current selection to the dashboard (matches today's behavior where both buttons just close).
- **Live while scrolling** - Dashboard mirrors every list tap live. Note: the modal covers the dashboard (BASE DMA discarded while open), so this isn't visible until close anyway.

**How should the committed selection be stored, given the gameplay engine will need it next?**

Options:
- **Shared selection module** - Add game/selection.{c,h} holding the committed {setlist,index,difficulty,mode} with getters. Song-select writes it; dashboard reads it; the gameplay engine reads it later. Cleaner seam for the engine.
- **Direct dashboard call** - Song-select calls ScreenDashboard_SetSong(index,difficulty,mode) directly; no shared module yet. Simpler now, revisit when wiring the engine.


**Answer:** SELECT commits, X cancels, Shared selection module
</details></tool-use>

# Map the selected song onto the dashboard SONG card

## Context

The user is building marvin's **gameplay engine**. The first step is to close the loop
between the **song-select modal** (`screen_song_select.c`) and the dashboard's **SONG
card**: when the operator picks a song + play-difficulty + game-mode and presses
**SELECT**, the dashboard card must show that song's artwork, metadata, tier, mode, and
difficulty. This gives the operator a persistent "now selected / ready to play" view and
establishes the **committed-selection state** the gameplay engine will read next.

The dashboard SONG card widgets already exist (MGS-generated in
`le_gen_screen_Marvin.{c,h}`); they carry figma placeholder text today. All the metadata,
artwork, and tier logic already exist in the song-select dialog — this task wires a
selection seam and reuses that logic.

**Naming convention (per user):** MGS dynamic labels end in camelCase
(`..._SongTitle`, `..._GameMode`); fixed labels are ALL-CAPS (`..._GENRE`, `..._MODE`) and
are left untouched.

Decisions confirmed with the user:
- **SELECT commits; X cancels.** The dashboard updates only on SELECT; the close (X)
  button dismisses without changing the card.
- **Shared selection module** holds the committed `{setlist, index, difficulty, mode}` so
  both the dashboard and the future gameplay engine read from one place.

## Dynamic dashboard widgets to drive (camelCase / artwork)

From `le_gen_screen_Marvin.h`, under `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD_SONG`:
- `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_AlbumArt` — `leImageWidget`, 144×144 → `Art_Small(setlist,index)`
- `Marvin_LABEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_SongTitle`, `_SongArtist`, `_SongAlbum`, `_SongGenre`,
  `_SongDuration`, `_SongTier`
- `Marvin_LABEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_GAMEPLAY_GameMode`
- `Marvin_LABEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_GAMEPLAY_Difficulty` (+ colored pill panel
  `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_GAMEPLAY_Difficulty` behind it)
- `Marvin_LABEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_Status` (MGS "READY") — **left as-is**; gameplay-driven later.

The card has no separate year label, so `SongAlbum` shows `"album - year"` (matches the
MGS placeholder "Inhuman Rampage - 2006"). ASCII only in dynamic strings — the DejaVu mono
subset is `0x20–0x7E, 0xA0–0xFF, 0x2605`, so no `•`/em-dash; the `★` (U+2605) tier glyph is
covered.

## Implementation

### 1. NEW `game/selection.{h,c}` — committed gameplay selection

Pure static state, no FreeRTOS/UI deps. Keyed on the recognizer's `(setlist, index)` so it
matches `Art_*`, `Catalog_Lookup`, and the future engine.

\```c
typedef enum { SEL_DIFF_EASY, SEL_DIFF_MEDIUM, SEL_DIFF_HARD, SEL_DIFF_EXPERT } sel_difficulty_t;
typedef enum { SEL_MODE_1P_ROBOT, SEL_MODE_1P_HUMAN, SEL_MODE_2P } sel_mode_t;

typedef struct {
    bool    valid;      /* false until the first Selection_Set */
    uint8_t setlist;    /* GP_SETLIST_* */
    uint8_t index;      /* song ordinal within setlist */
    uint8_t difficulty; /* sel_difficulty_t */
    uint8_t mode;       /* sel_mode_t */
} selection_t;

void              Selection_Set(uint8_t setlist, uint8_t index, uint8_t difficulty, uint8_t mode);
const selection_t *Selection_Get(void);

# Map the selected song onto the dashboard SONG card

## Context

The user is building marvin's **gameplay engine**. The first step is to close the loop
between the **song-select modal** (`screen_song_select.c`) and the dashboard's **SONG
card**: when the operator picks a song + play-difficulty + game-mode and presses
**SELECT**, the dashboard card must show that song's artwork, metadata, tier, mode, and
difficulty. This gives the operator a persistent "now selected / ready to play" view and
establishes the **committed-selection state** the gameplay engine will read next.

The dashboard SONG card widgets already exist (MGS-generated in
`le_gen_screen_Marvin.{c,h}`); they carry figma placeholder text today. All the metadata,
artwork, and tier logic already exist in the song-select dialog — this task wires a
selection seam and reuses that logic.

**Naming convention (per user):** MGS dynamic labels end in camelCase
(`..._SongTitle`, `..._GameMode`); fixed labels are ALL-CAPS (`..._GENRE`, `..._MODE`) and
are left untouched.

Decisions confirmed with the user:
- **SELECT commits; X cancels.** The dashboard updates only on SELECT; the close (X)
  button dismisses without changing the card.
- **Shared selection module** holds the committed `{setlist, index, difficulty, mode}` so
  both the dashboard and the future gameplay engine read from one place.

```h
#ifndef MARVIN_GAME_SELECTION_H
#define MARVIN_GAME_SELECTION_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* Committed gameplay selection: the song + play difficulty + game mode the
 * operator confirmed in the song-select dialog (SELECT). Keyed on the
 * recognizer's stable (setlist, index) so it lines up with Art_* / Catalog_* and
 * the gameplay engine. Pure static state (no FreeRTOS/UI deps); single observer
 * for the UI to mirror it. Static zero-init leaves valid=false until the first
 * Selection_Set, so no explicit initialize call is needed. */

typedef enum
{
    SEL_DIFF_EASY = 0,
    SEL_DIFF_MEDIUM,
    SEL_DIFF_HARD,
    SEL_DIFF_EXPERT
} sel_difficulty_t;

typedef enum
{
    SEL_MODE_1P_ROBOT = 0,
    SEL_MODE_1P_HUMAN,
    SEL_MODE_2P
} sel_mode_t;

typedef struct
{
    bool    valid;      /* false until the first Selection_Set */
    uint8_t setlist;    /* GP_SETLIST_* */
    uint8_t index;      /* song ordinal within its setlist */
    uint8_t difficulty; /* sel_difficulty_t */
    uint8_t mode;       /* sel_mode_t */
} selection_t;

/* Commit a selection and notify the observer (if any). */
void Selection_Set(uint8_t setlist, uint8_t index, uint8_t difficulty, uint8_t mode);

/* The current committed selection; ->valid is false before the first Set. */
const selection_t *Selection_Get(void);

/* Register the single observer, invoked on every Selection_Set with the new
 * selection. NULL clears it. */
void Selection_SetObserver(void (*cb)(const selection_t *));

#endif /* MARVIN_GAME_SELECTION_H */

```

```c
#include "game/selection.h"

static selection_t s_sel;
static void (*s_observer)(const selection_t *);

void Selection_Set(uint8_t setlist, uint8_t index, uint8_t difficulty, uint8_t mode)
{
    s_sel.setlist    = setlist;
    s_sel.index      = index;
    s_sel.difficulty = difficulty;
    s_sel.mode       = mode;
    s_sel.valid      = true;

    if (s_observer != NULL) { s_observer(&s_sel); }
}

const selection_t *Selection_Get(void)
{
    return &s_sel;
}

void Selection_SetObserver(void (*cb)(const selection_t *))
{
    s_observer = cb;
}

```

```c
#include "ui/song_detail.h"

#include <stdio.h>

int SongDetail_Tier(const char *difficulty)
{
    const char *d = difficulty;
    if (d != NULL && d[0] >= '1' && d[0] <= '8' && d[1] == '\0') { return d[0] - '0'; }
    return 0;
}

void SongDetail_TierText(int tier, char *buf, size_t n)
{
    size_t p = 0;
    if (tier <= 0) { (void)snprintf(buf, n, "BONUS"); return; }
    for (int i = 0; i < tier && p + 3u < n; i++)
    {
        buf[p++] = (char)0xE2; buf[p++] = (char)0x98; buf[p++] = (char)0x85;   /* U+2605 ★ */
    }
    (void)snprintf(buf + p, n - p, " TIER %d", tier);
}

const leScheme *SongDetail_TierScheme(int tier)
{
    switch (tier)
    {
        case 1:  return &SCHEME_TEXT_TIER_1;
        case 2:  return &SCHEME_TEXT_TIER_2;
        case 3:  return &SCHEME_TEXT_TIER_3;
        case 4:  return &SCHEME_TEXT_TIER_4;
        case 5:  return &SCHEME_TEXT_TIER_5;
        case 6:  return &SCHEME_TEXT_TIER_6;
        case 7:  return &SCHEME_TEXT_TIER_7;
        case 8:  return &SCHEME_TEXT_TIER_8;
        default: return &SCHEME_TEXT_GRAY_D4D4D8;   /* bonus / unknown → light gray */
    }
}

void SongDetail_Duration(uint16_t length_s, char *buf, size_t n)
{
    if (length_s != 0u)
    {
        (void)snprintf(buf, n, "%u:%02u",
                       (unsigned)(length_s / 60u), (unsigned)(length_s % 60u));
    }
    else { (void)snprintf(buf, n, "-"); }
}

```

#ifndef MARVIN_UTIL_LEGATO_UTF8_H
#define MARVIN_UTIL_LEGATO_UTF8_H

#include <stdint.h>

#include "gfx/legato/legato.h"   /* leChar, leString, leResult */

/* UTF-8 helpers for Legato strings. Legato's setFromCStr and the C-string
 * renderer are byte-oriented: each input byte becomes one leChar/glyph, so a
 * multibyte UTF-8 sequence renders as several glyphs. These decode UTF-8 into
 * leChar code points first. leChar is uint16_t, so code points are limited to
 * the BMP (U+0000..U+FFFF); anything higher stops the decode. */

/* Decode utf8 into out[] as code points. Writes at most cap code points and
 * returns the count written. Stops at the NUL, on a malformed byte, or when
 * cap is reached. */
uint32_t utf8_to_lechar(const char *utf8, leChar *out, uint32_t cap);

/* Set any leString (fixed or dynamic) from a UTF-8 C string, decoding
 * multibyte sequences into single code points. Use instead of
 * str->fn->setFromCStr for text that may contain non-ASCII characters. */
leResult lestring_set_utf8(leString *str, const char *utf8);

#endif

174	 * offsetting the frame base to the active top-left, sizing HEOCFG4 to the active
175	 * w/h, and skipping the cropped columns each line via XSTRIDE. Full-frame until
176	 * detection locks (safe fallback). The matching BASE DMA-discard behind the opaque
177	 * video is set by base_discard_reconcile (single DISCEN owner). Seeds HEO with the
178	 * latest frame (0 until the first frame, which heo_frame_latch then fixes within a
179	 * frame-time). Video-task ctx. */
180	static void heo_bind(uint16_t src_w, uint16_t src_h,
181	                     uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h)
182	{
183	    if (x + dst_w > BASE_W || y + dst_h > BASE_H)
184	    {
185	        LOG_WARN("UI: video window %lux%lu @(%lu,%lu) exceeds panel; skip bind\r\n",
186	                 (unsigned long)dst_w, (unsigned long)dst_h,
187	                 (unsigned long)x, (unsigned long)y);
188	        return;
189	    }
190	
191	    Video_FrameInfo fi;
192	    Video_GetFrameInfo(&fi);
193	
194	    /* Active picture crop within the full frame (full-frame fallback pre-lock). */
195	    uint16_t ax, ay, aw, ah;
196	    (void)Video_GetActiveRect(&ax, &ay, &aw, &ah);
197	    uint32_t bpp        = fi.bytes_per_pixel;
198	    uint32_t stride     = (uint32_t)src_w * bpp;                 /* full line bytes */
199	    uint32_t crop_off   = (uint32_t)ay * stride + (uint32_t)ax * bpp;
200	    uint32_t addr       = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)fi.buffer + crop_off;
201	
202	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, false, true);
203	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888_PACKED, false);
204	    /* Re-apply the levels CLUT enable (RGBColorMode clears GAM); off = raw pass-through. */
205	    if (s_video_levels) { XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG1 |=  LCDC_HEOCFG1_GAM_Msk; }
206	    else                { XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG1 &= ~LCDC_HEOCFG1_GAM_Msk; }
207	    XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, addr, false);
208	    XLCDC_SetLayerXStride(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, (uint32_t)(src_w - aw) * bpp, false);
209	    XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, x, y, false);
210	
211	    /* Display rect (HEOCFG3, dst) vs source-memory rect (HEOCFG4, active crop):
212	     * equal for 1:1, differ when scaling. Written directly — XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYSize
213	     * sets both equal. */
214	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG3 = LCDC_HEOCFG3_XSIZE(dst_w - 1u) | LCDC_HEOCFG3_YSIZE(dst_h - 1u);
215	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG4 = LCDC_HEOCFG4_XMEMSIZE(aw - 1u) | LCDC_HEOCFG4_YMEMSIZE(ah - 1u);
216	
217	    bool scaling = (dst_w != aw) || (dst_h != ah);
218	    if (scaling)
219	    {
220	        uint32_t hf = scaler_factor(aw, dst_w);
221	        uint32_t vf = scaler_factor(ah, dst_h);
222	
223	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG23 = LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSYEN(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSCEN(1)
224	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSYEN(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSCEN(1);
225	        /* Bicubic luma + chroma, both planes (mirrors MCC's surface-set path). */
226	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG30 = LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSYCFG(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSYBICU(1)
227	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSCCFG(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSCBICU(1);
228	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG31 = LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSYCFG(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSYBICU(1)
229	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSCCFG(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSCBICU(1);
230	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG24 = LCDC_HEOCFG24_VXSYFACT(vf);
231	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG25 = LCDC_HEOCFG25_VXSCFACT(vf);
232	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG26 = LCDC_HEOCFG26_HXSYFACT(hf);
233	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG27 = LCDC_HEOCFG27_HXSCFACT(hf);
234	    }
235	    else
236	    {
237	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG23 = LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSYEN(0) | LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSCEN(0)
238	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSYEN(0) | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSCEN(0);
239	    }
240	
241	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, true, true);
242	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_BASE, true, true);
243	
244	    s_heo_crop_off = crop_off;
245	    s_bound_src_w = src_w; s_bound_src_h = src_h;
246	    s_bound_ax = ax; s_bound_ay = ay; s_bound_aw = aw; s_bound_ah = ah;
247	    LOG_INFO("UI: HEO bound src %ux%u active %ux%u@(%u,%u) -> dst %lux%lu @(%lu,%lu) %s\r\n",
248	             (unsigned)src_w, (unsigned)src_h, (unsigned)aw, (unsigned)ah, (unsigned)ax, (unsigned)ay,
249	             (unsigned long)dst_w, (unsigned long)dst_h,

#include "ui/screens/album_art/screen_album_art.h"

#include "ui/ui_manager.h"   /* CANVAS_ALBUM_ART */
#include "gfx/canvas/gfx_canvas_api.h"

/* Layer 3 is RGBA8888 — the only full-color mode the 2D engine supports
 * (gfx2dFormats[]: RGB_565 and RGBA_8888 only; RGB_888 is unsupported, so a 24bpp
 * canvas can't be GFX2D-blitted and renders garbage). At 508x208 the 32bpp surface
 * is ~0.42 MB, so the bandwidth cost is trivial; the dialog itself (OVR1) stays
 * RGB565. The window sits over the dialog's art rect. */
#define ART_W   508u
#define ART_H   208u
#define ART_X   433    /* absolute screen position of the art rect (over the OVR1 dialog) */
#define ART_Y   160

#define FB_NOCACHE   __attribute__((section(".region_nocache"), aligned (32)))

/* Non-cached so the LCDC scans CPU-/2D-written pixels coherently (like the other
 * canvas surfaces). RGBA8888: 4 B/px. */
static uint32_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb_album_art[ART_W * ART_H];

void ScreenAlbumArt_InitSurface(void)
{
    /* Clear to opaque black. The buffer is NOLOAD (uninitialized DDR = noise), and
     * the album-art panel is BACKGROUND_NONE, so any area Legato doesn't paint would
     * scan as garbage; a known fill makes "unpainted" read as black, not noise.
     * RGBA8888 word is 0xRRGGBBAA, so opaque black = 0x000000FF. */
    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < (ART_W * ART_H); i++) { s_fb_album_art[i] = 0x000000FFu; }

    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_ALBUM_ART, ART_W, ART_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, s_fb_album_art);
}

void ScreenAlbumArt_Setup(void)
{
    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_ALBUM_ART, ART_W, ART_H);
    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_ALBUM_ART, ART_X, ART_Y);
}

In this case a Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) server will automatically assign an IP address to the board and the PC. (Ensure there are no IT restrictions for plugging the board on the local network)\n\n## Setup\n{{step n=\u00221\u0022}}\n    Download the image\n\n{{substep n=\u00221\u0022}}\nDownload the Yocto Project\u003Csup\u003E\u00AE\u003C/sup\u003E image from the [image-link](https://files.linux4sam.org/pub/demo/linux4sam-2024.04/linux4sam-poky-sam9x75_curiosity-headless-2024.04.img.bz2) repository.\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00222\u0022}}\nPlace in any directory of your choice.\n{{/substep}}\n{{/step}}\n\n----\n\n{{step n=\u00222\u0022}}\nCopy the downloaded file into the SD memory card using balenaEtcher.\n\n{{substep n=\u00221\u0022}}\nInsert the SD memory card into the PC.\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00222\u0022}}\nDownload, install and run **[balenaEtcher](https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/bin/view/url:https://etcher/balena/io/)**.\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00223\u0022 img=\u0022select-image.bmp\u0022 alt=\u0022balenaEtcher window Flash from File button\u0022}}\nSelect the downloaded **[linux4sam-poky-sam9x75_curiosity-headless-2024.10.img.bz2(% contenteditable=\u0022false\u0022 style=\u0022--darkreader-inline-bgcolor:var(--darkreader-background-dcdcdc80, rgba(31, 35, 37, 0.5)); --darkreader-inline-bgimage:initial; background:rgba(220, 220, 220, 0.5); display:none\u0022 tabindex=\u0022-1\u0022 %)~\\[~\\[image:data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw==~|~|draggable=\u0022true\u0022 height=\u002215\u0022 role=\u0022presentation\u0022 title=\u0022Click and drag to move\u0022 width=\u002215\u0022~\\]~\\]](https://files.linux4sam.org/pub/demo/linux4sam-2024.10/linux4sam-poky-sam9x75_curiosity-headless-2024.10.img.bz2)(%%)**.\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00224\u0022 img=\u0022choose-target.bmp\u0022 alt=\u0022balenaEtcher window Select Target button\u0022}}\nClick **Select target **to download.\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00225\u0022 img=\u0022select-target.bmp\u0022 alt=\u0022balenaEtcher  Select target window\u0022}}\nSelect the mounted SD card.\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00226\u0022 img=\u0022flash.bmp\u0022 alt=\u0022balenaEtcher window Flash button\u0022}}\nSelect **Flash**.\n\nThe SD card will be ready for use once flashing is completed.\n{{/substep}}\n{{/step}}\n\n----\n\n{{step n=\u00223\u0022}}\n##### Connect the components as described in the following steps:\n{{substep n=\u00221\u0022}}\n##### Ethernet cable to J5 connector on the LAN8840 EDS2 Daughter Card EV12N54A.\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00222\u0022}}\n##### Other side of the Ethernet cable shall be plugged in the PC (network configuration 1) or in a wall plug/router (network configuration 2).\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00223\u0022}}\n##### SD card inserted on the SD Boot **J14** slot.\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00224\u0022}}\n##### Serial USB dongle to UART DEBUG **J35** header.\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00225\u0022}}\n##### USB Type-A to Micro-USB cable to **J2** Micro-USB port for power.\n![Connection setup](https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/download/attachments/hardware-updated.jpg)\n{{/substep}}\n{{/step}}\n\n## Set Up the SAM9X75 Curiosity Board Serial Terminal and Start the iPerf3 TCP Server\n{{step n=\u00224\u0022}}\nSet up SAM9X75 Curiosity Board Serial Terminal on the PC.\n\n{{substep n=\u00221\u0022}}\nIdentify the serial USB connection by monitoring the last lines of **dmesg **command (may need sudo rights).\n\nThe /dev/ttyUSBx number will be used to configure the terminal emulator.\n\n![dmesg output](https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/download/attachments/dmesg_output.jpg)\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00222\u0022}}\nOn the PC, open your favorite terminal emulator with the following settings:\n\n- Baud Rate: **115200**\n- Data:** 8-bit**\n- Parity: **None**\n- Stop: **1-bit**\n- Flow Control: **None**\n\nFor example with picocom, assuming the serial USB interface is /dev/ttyUSB0:\n\n{{code}}\nsudo picocom -b 115200 /dev/ttyUSB0  (sudo rights may be needed)\n{{/code}}\n{{/substep}}\n{{/step}}\n\n----\n\n{{step n=\u00225\u0022}}\n##### Press the **RESET (SW3)** button on the SAM9X75 Curiosity Board to force a reset.\n##### When the system is ready, the SAM9X75 serial Terminal set up in Step 4 will show a prompt. This is the TCP Server terminal.\n{{substep n=\u00221\u0022}}\n Verify the login prompt is shown on the SAM9X75 serial Terminal.\n\n![TCP Server terminal](https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/download/attachments/linux-iperf-demo-prompt.jpg)\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00222\u0022}}\nEnter \u0022**root**\u0022 to log in. No password is required.\n\nIn case you do not see the prompt, press the **enter **key to force the prompt to refresh.\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00223\u0022}}\n- In network configuration 1:\n**  Without a DHCP server, a static IP address (for example **192.168.100.11** here) needs to be assigned to the board with the following command:\n\n{{code}}\n# ifconfig eth0 192.168.100.11 netmask 255.255.255.0\n\n{{/code}}\n\n- In network configuration 2:\n** Getting a lease with the DHCP server should be automatic. To make sure, type \u0022**udhcpc**\u0022 in the command line:\n\n{{code}}\n# udhcpc\n\n{{/code}}\n\n![TCP Server](https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/download/attachments/tcp-server-udhcp.jpg)\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00224\u0022}}\nFinally, type \u0022**ifconfig**\u0022** **on the command line and verify the internet address is assigned to the SAM9X75 Curiosity Board.\n\n{{code}}\n# ifconfig\n\n{{/code}}\n\n![ifconfig](https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/download/attachments/ifconfig_9x75.png)\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00225\u0022}}\nNote the assigned IP address as it will be used to run the iPerf3 test.\n\nIn this example, the IP address is **192.168.100.11** in network configuration 1 and **10.14.63.85** in network configuration 2. It will be different in your environment.\n{{/substep}}\n{{/step}}\n\n----\n\n{{step n=\u00226\u0022}}\n##### Start the iPerf3 TCP Server on the SAM9X75 Curiosity Board by running the following command:\n{{code}}\n# iperf3 -s -i 1\n\n{{/code}}\n{{/step}}\n\n## Configure the Linux PC and start the iPerf3 TCP Client\n{{step n=\u00227\u0022}}\n Open a Linux terminal program on the PC:\n\n![Run Linux Terminal Program](https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/download/attachments/1717103504592-712.png)\n{{/step}}\n\n----\n\n{{step n=\u00228\u0022}}\nComplete the following for network configuration 1 and network configuration 2.\n\n{{substep n=\u00221\u0022}}\nIn network configuration 1:\n\nThe PC Ethernet IP address and mask must be manually configured (sudo rights are needed).\n\n(% style=\u0022margin:0px; padding:0px\u0022 %)First, use the **ifconfig** command to find out the name of the PC Ethernet interface. In this example, we will consider it is eth0.\n\nIf the board IP is **192.168.100.11**, then, for example configure the PC IP with **192.168.100.2/255.255.255.0** with the following command:\n\n{{code language=\u0022html\u0022}}\n# ifconfig eth0 192.168.100.2 netmask 255.255.255.0\n\n{{/code}}\n{{/substep}}\n\n{{substep n=\u00222\u0022}}\nIn network configuration 2:\n\nNo manual change is needed; the DHCP will automatically assign the right IP address.\n{{/substep}}\n{{/step}}\n\n----\n\n{{step n=\u00229\u0022}}\n##### In the PC terminal, start the TCP Client iPerf3 with the following command:\n{{info}}\nNote that the IP address below used must match the IP address recorded in Step 5.5.\n{{/info}}\n\n{{code language=\u0022html\u0022}}\n# iperf3 -c 192.168.100.11 -i 1 -t 5\n\n{{/code}}\n\nThis will test the performance of the network transfers between the PC (TCP Client) and the SAM9X75 Curiosity Board (TCP Server).\n{{/step}}\n\n----\n\n{{step n=\u002210\u0022}}\n##### Come back to the SAM9X75 serial terminal and confirm the test results:\n![TCP Server terminal](https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/download/attachments/tcp-server-iperf3.jpg)\n{{/step}}\n\n----\n\n{{step n=\u002211\u0022}}\nCongratulations! Your SAM9X75 board running Linux is now connected over Ethernet to your PC.\n\nWhat\u0027s next? See the following sections for more resources.\n{{/step}}\n\n## Troubleshooting\n### Common\n|(% style=\u0022width:506px\u0022 %)The SAM9X75 serial terminal is not showing anything.|(% style=\u0022width:861px\u0022 %)\u003E There are multiple possible reasons why the terminal does not show anything:\r\n\u003E\r\n\u003E * Verify that the RX-TX signals of the serial cable are properly connected to the RX-TX signals of the board.\r\n\u003E * Verify that the ground signal is properly connected.\r\n\u003E * Verify that the SD card contains the right files.\n|(% style=\u0022width:506px\u0022 %)\u003E Running iPerf3 command in the PC terminal results in Connection refused error.\r\n\u003E\r\n\u003E [  1] tcp connect to 10.14.63.70 port 5001 failed (Connection refused) on 2024-05-31 11:43:21 (US Mountain Standard Time).|(% style=\u0022width:861px\u0022 %)Verify the IP address used when sending the iPerf3 command matches the target IP address.\n|(% style=\u0022width:506px\u0022 %)Terminal shows RomBoot message.|(% style=\u0022width:861px\u0022 %)\u003E * Verify if the SD card contains the right files.\r\n\u003E * Verify that the SD card is inserted properly.\n|IT restrictions forbid the plugging of SD cards in the PC. BalenaEtcher can\u0027t be used. |\u003E Another option for programming the SD Card is to use the Microchip [SAM-BA\u003Csup\u003E\u00AE\u003C/sup\u003E In-system Programmer (ISP)](https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/bin/view/url:https://www/microchip/com/en-us/development-tool/sam-ba-in-system-programmer) tool.\r\n\u003E\r\n\u003E 1. Download and install [SAM-BA ISP](https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/bin/view/url:https://www/microchip/com/en-us/development-tool/sam-ba-in-system-programmer) (v3.9 at least).\r\n\u003E 1. Decompress the downloaded Linux bz2 image.\r\n\u003E 1. Plug the USB Type-A to Micro-USB cable from the PC to** J2** Micro-USB port for power and SAM-BA ISP connection.\r\n\u003E 1. Plug the SD card in the SAM9X75 board (no more in the PC) and use the following SAM-BA ISP command to program the SD Card:\r\n\u003E\r\n\u003E **.\\sam-ba -p serial -b sam9x75-curiosity -a sdmmc -c write:linux4sam-poky-sam9x75\\_curiosity-headless-2024.04.img**\n\n## Learn More\n- [SAM9X75 Curiosity LAN Kit](https://www.microchip.com/en-us/development-tool/EV31H43A) (User Guide, Design Files)\n- [LAN8840 EDS2 Daughter Card](https://www.microchip.com/en-us/development-tool/EV12N54A) (User Guide, Design Files)\n- [SAM9X75 Product Page](https://www.microchip.com/en-us/product/sam9x75) (Datasheet, Errata)\n- [MPLAB\u00AE Harmony v3 Solutions](https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/bin/view/path:https://github/com/search?q=org%3AMicrochip-MPLAB-Harmony\u002Bsam_9x7\u0026type=repositories)\n- [MPLAB Discover Code Examples](https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/bin/view/path:https://mplab-discover/microchip/com/v2/category/com/microchip/code/examples?dsl=9x75)\n- [Linux Solutions](https://www.linux4sam.org/bin/view/Linux4SAM/Sam9x75CuriosityMainPage)","url":"https://developerhelp.microchip.com/xwiki/bin/view/software-tools/mcu-dev-boards/32-bit-kits/sam9x75-ev-curiosity/lan-kit-get-started-linux/?utm_source=mchpmcp","keywords":["SAM9X75 Curiosity LAN Kit - Quick Start Guide for Linux\u00AE"],"relevancyScore":40.181538},{"title":"SAM9X75","content":"# Device: SAM9X75\n\n## SAM9X75 Summary\n\nThe SAM9X75 MPU is a high-performance cost-optimized ARM926EJ-S CPU-based embedded MPU running up to 800MHz supporting MIPI-DSI, LVDS and RGB display interfaces w/ 2D graphics acceleration, Gigabit Ethernet w/ TSN and CAN-FD. The MPUs offer advanced security functions, like tamper detection, secure boot, secure key storage, TRNG, PUF as well as higher-performance crypto accelerators for AES and SHA. The SAM9X75 series is supported by Microchip\u0027s Mainline Linux distribution as well as Microchip MPLAB Harmony development tools for bare-metal/RTOS support. SAM9X75 is well-suited for industrial and medical applications with or w/o graphical displays up to 1024 x 768, as well as home automation and security system gateways including access control with biometrics. Microchip offers for different supply configurations, fully tested power management solutions respecting the SAM9X75 power sequencing specifications that are referenced in the product specification.\n\n## SAM9X75 Features\n\nLow System Cost and High Value Integration:- 800MHz ARM926EJ-S Core, 266MHz System/Memory Bus\n\nMemories:- 32 KB Data Cache and 32 KB Instruction Cache\n- 64 KB internal SRAM\n- 16-bit DDR databus\n\nEnhanced User Interface capability:- 24-bit LCD Controller with overlays up to 1024 x 768 resolution\n- 2D Graphics Engine\n- LVDS Display Interface\n- RGB 24-bit display interface\n- MIPI-DSI Display interface\n\nCamera Support- Parallel Port\n- MIPI CSI-2 Camera interface\n\nBuilt-in Class D Amplifier\n\nLarge number of connectivity options:- Single 10/100/1G Ethernet\n- One Quad/Octal SPI controller\n- Thirteen FLEXCOMs (USART, SPI and TWI/I2C)\n- Two High-speed USB Host \u002B One High-speed Host or Device\n\nFully-Integrated Security:- Secure Boot with on-chip Secure Key Storage (OTP)\n- Hardware Encryption Engine (TDES, AES and SHA), True Random Generator (TRNG), PUF\n- Physical protection against tamper, 8 tamper detection pins\n- On the Fly scrambling / unscrambling for memories\n\nRich Development Ecosystem:- Free mainline Linux\u00AE Distribution\n- MPLAB\u00AE X Integrated Development Environment and MPLAB\u00AE Harmony v3\n- Multiple Third-party Software and Hardware Solutions\n\nOptimized for Easy PCB Design and Low EMI- TFBGA240, 11x11, 0.65 mm pitch - de-populated ball-out\n- TFBGA256, 9x9, 0.5 mm pitch - de-populated ball-out\n- Power/GND balls placed and distributed for optimal decoupling\n- Fractional System PLL, I/Os slew rate and drive control, DDR I/Os calibration for Low EMI\n\n## SAM9X75 Documents\n\n- \\*\\*Data Sheet\\*\\*: [SAM9X7 Series Data Sheet](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/MPU32/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/SAM9X7-Series-DS60001813.pdf)\n- \\*\\*Errata\\*\\*: [SAM9X7 Series Silicon Errata and Data Sheet Clarifications](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/MPU32/ProductDocuments/Errata/SAM9X7-Series-Silicon-Errata-and-Data-Sheet-Clarifications-DS80001082.pdf)\n\n## SAM9X75 Code are a set of extensions that integrate the MPLAB development ecosystem with VS Code, offering a seamless and efficient environment for developing designs based on Microchip devices.\n\\*\\*URL\\*\\*: [https://www.microchip.com/en-us/development-tool/MPLAB-Extensions](https://www.microchip.com/en-us/development-tool/MPLAB-Extensions)\n\n### MPLAB XC32 COMPILER\nWhen debugger/programmer enables quick prototyping and portable, production-ready programming for all Microchip devices, including PIC\u00AE microcontrollers (MCUs) and dsPIC\u00AE Digital Signal Controllers (DSCs), AVR\u00AE and SAM devices and Arm\u00AE Cortex\u00AE-based microprocessors (MPUs).\n\\*\\*URL\\*\\*: Implementation Example - SAM9X75 Hardware Design Considerations","content":"# 3.2.2 Implementation Example The SAM9X75 was especially engineered to be placed on a four-layer PCB. To achieve the best performance, we recommend using the following layer stack-up and line width and clearances. This stack-up was chosen because it can provide all the required impedances by using minimum 100 \u00B5m-wide traces. The minimum trace width is 100 \u00B5m (~4 mil) which is relatively standard nowadays for PCB manufacturers. This also ensures that the routing does not take much space on the board.\\n\\n Images: https://onlinedocs.microchip.com/oxy/GUID-8614E0F2-FF39-49AC-BB53-2AAE155D93DA-en-US-2/GUID-A4184872-D681-4D78-ADD0-94EF20B2157C-high.pdf#toolbar=1","url":"https://onlinedocs.microchip.com/oxy/GUID-8614E0F2-FF39-49AC-BB53-2AAE155D93DA-en-US-2/GUID-BB70DF2F-8561-4C8A-A986-22077730AD09.html?utm_source=mchpmcp","keywords":["3.2.2 Implementation Example - SAM9X75 Hardware Design Considerations","SAM9X75 Hardware Design Considerations"],"relevancyScore":49.863937},{"title":"3 Layout Checklist Description and Examples - SAM9X75 Hardware Design Considerations","content":"# 3 Layout Checklist Description and Examples This section describes each item in the layout checklist and provides implementation examples. I've mapped the constraint fully. Here's what I found before proposing options:

- **Only 4 display layers exist** in the MCC plib (`BASE, HEO, OVR1, OVR2`) — no 5th is exposed. The SAM9X7 does have a hardware cursor block, but it's unconfigured by MCC and capped (~128×128), so it'd be raw-register work outside MCC.
- The small art is **already decoded to RGBA8888** in DDR ([art.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/art.c) slots, opaque alpha forced), and it's **already blitting into the RGB565 base fine** — so the thumbnail works today, just reduced to 16-bit depth. This is a fidelity gap, not a broken render.
- The thumbnail sits at abs **(297, 586), 144×144**. OVR2 is **free exactly when the plain dashboard is the top view** — nav (OVR2) and song-select (OVR2 album strip) are both transient modals. So OVR2 is available in the common case; it's only "taken" while a drawer/dialog is up.

That last point is the crux: OVR2 *can* host the thumbnail, with the RGB565 base version as a fallback for the brief moments nav/song-select borrow the layer.

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

def to565_roundtrip(im):
    """888 -> RGB565 (round) -> 888 (bit-replication expand), what the panel shows."""
    im = im.convert("RGB")
    px = im.load()
    out = Image.new("RGB", im.size)
    op = out.load()
    for y in range(im.size[1]):
        for x in range(im.size[0]):
            r,g,b = px[x,y]
            # quantize with rounding to 5/6/5
            r5 = min(31, (r*31 + 127)//255)
            g6 = min(63, (g*63 + 127)//255)
            b5 = min(31, (b*31 + 127)//255)
            # expand back by bit replication (hardware 565->888)
            R = (r5<<3)|(r5>>2)
            G = (g6<<2)|(g6>>4)
            B = (b5<<3)|(b5>>2)
            op[x,y]=(R,G,B)
    return out

CELL=144
PAD=10
LBL=22
cols=len(picks)
W = cols*CELL + (cols+1)*PAD
H = LBL + 3*CELL + 4*PAD + 2*LBL
canvas = Image.new("RGB",(W,H),(24,24,27))
d=ImageDraw.Draw(canvas)
try: font=ImageFont.truetype("/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Arial.ttf",14)
except: font=ImageFont.load_default()

def label(x,y,t): d.text((x,y),t,fill=(210,210,215),font=font)

y0=LBL
for r,(name,rowlbl) in enumerate([("888","original RGBA8888"),("565","RGB565 round-trip"),("diff","abs diff x4")]):
    ry = y0 + r*(CELL+PAD) + (LBL if r>0 else 0)
    label(PAD, ry-16 if r==0 else ry-16, rowlbl)
    for c,p in enumerate(picks):
        cx = PAD + c*(CELL+PAD)
        im = Image.open(p).convert("RGB").resize((CELL,CELL))
        if name=="888":
            cell=im
            if r==0: label(cx, 2, os.path.basename(p))
        elif name=="565":
            cell=to565_roundtrip(im)
        else:
            q=to565_roundtrip(im)
            import PIL.ImageChops as C
            cell=C.multiply(C.difference(im,q), Image.new("RGB",im.size,(4,4,4)))
        canvas.paste(cell,(cx,ry))

out="/tmp/claude/art_565_vs_888.png"
canvas.save(out)
print("wrote", out, canvas.size)
PY
uv run /tmp/claude/cmp565.py 2>&1 | tail -5

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 20:54:07Z)**_

Here's the honest read from the comparison (top = 888 original, middle = RGB565 round-trip as the panel would show it, bottom = per-pixel abs error amplified **14×**):

**On real covers, RGB565 is visually indistinguishable from 888.** Look at the middle row — Pearl Jam, Disturbed, Héroes del Silencio, GH3 — none show banding you'd notice. The ×14-amplified diff row is almost black with only faint scattered dither noise in the darkest smooth areas (Pearl Jam's red backdrop). Photographic cover art has enough texture/grain to mask 16-bit quantization.

**Banding only bites on smooth synthetic gradients** — the leftmost swatch. Its 565 version shows real contour bands, and its diff row shows a strong regular banding pattern. That's the worst case.

The key implication: the **small dashboard thumbnail is a photographic cover with no baked gradient**, so it lands firmly in the "indistinguishable" bucket. The one asset in this project that *does* have a smooth gradient is the **large song-select strip** (baked difficulty fade) — which is exactly why that one already gets its own dedicated RGBA8888 layer (CANVAS_ALBUM_ART on OVR2). The dashboard thumbnail has no equivalent gradient to band.

## Recommendation

**Keep the dashboard thumbnail at RGB565 (do nothing).** The fidelity gain from an OVR2 multiplex doesn't show up on real covers, and you'd pay for it with rebind bookkeeping on every nav/dialog transition plus a visible 8888→565 pop on the right-side thumbnail while the nav drawer is open. Not worth it for zero perceptible gain.

If you ever swap in smooth-gradient thumbnails (or bake a difficulty fade into the small tier like the large one), banding would appear — and the OVR2-multiplex-with-565-fallback is the ready fallback at that point.

So: is the thumbnail actually rendering correctly for you at 565 right now (just wanted it sharper), or is it showing something wrong/blank? That tells me whether we're done here or chasing an actual blit bug.
