54	# screen_song_select.c, so keep them in sync. Edit a row to retune one tier.
55	TIER_COLORS = {
56	    1: (0x4A, 0xDE, 0x53),   # green
57	    2: (0x14, 0xB8, 0xA6),   # teal
58	    3: (0x3B, 0x82, 0xF6),   # blue
59	    4: (0xA8, 0x55, 0xF7),   # purple
60	    5: (0xFA, 0xCC, 0x15),   # yellow
61	    6: (0xFB, 0x92, 0x3C),   # orange
62	    7: (0xFF, 0x56, 0x30),   # red-orange
63	    8: (0xEF, 0x44, 0x44),   # red
64	}
65	BONUS_GRAY = (96, 96, 96)
66	
67	# Fade tunables (visual taste; safe to adjust). A single full-height ramp by height
68	# fraction t: the difficulty `color` washes the top and darkens to a near-black tint
69	# of the same hue at the bottom edge. FADE_GAMMA shapes it (>1 keeps the top clean
70	# and concentrates the darkening into the lower band). FADE_START/FADE_FULL bound the
71	# ramp; the defaults (0..1) run it across the whole height.
72	FADE_TOP_ALPHA   = 0.35   # wash opacity at the top (0 = no tint, art fully visible)
73	FADE_START       = 0.00   # height fraction where darkening begins (raise to keep more clean top)
74	FADE_FULL        = 1.00   # height fraction reaching darkest (1.0 = at the bottom edge)
75	FADE_BOTTOM_DARK = 0.05   # darkest color = difficulty color * this (same hue, ~black)
76	FADE_GAMMA       = 2.00   # ramp shape: >1 keeps the top lighter, darkens lower down
77	
78	
79	def load_difficulty(catalog_path):
80	    """Read songs.csv into {(setlist, index): difficulty_string}."""
81	    table = {}
82	    p = Path(catalog_path)
83	    if not p.is_file():
84	        print(f"WARNING: catalog {catalog_path} not found; all fades will be gray.",
85	              file=sys.stderr)
86	        return table
87	    with p.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
88	        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
89	            try:
90	                key = (row["setlist"].strip(), int(row["index"]))
91	            except (KeyError, ValueError):
92	                continue
93	            table[key] = (row.get("difficulty") or "").strip()
94	    return table
95	
96	
97	def difficulty_color(diff_str):
98	    """Map a difficulty string to its tier color: "1".."8" -> TIER_COLORS,
99	    anything else (e.g. "bonus", empty) -> gray."""
100	    try:
101	        tier = int(diff_str)
102	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
103	        tier = None
104	    return TIER_COLORS.get(tier, BONUS_GRAY)
105	
106	
107	def build_fade(w, h, color):
108	    """Vertical gradient overlay baked over the cover: the difficulty `color`
109	    washes the top of the strip, darkens through the middle, and goes to a solid
110	    dark tint of the same hue over the lower band so the title/artist text sits on
111	    a legible, on-theme backdrop.
112	
113	    Returns (overlay_rgb, alpha) as full-size images for
114	    Image.composite(overlay_rgb, image, alpha). Per row, by height fraction t:
115	      - t <= FADE_START          : top wash (alpha FADE_TOP_ALPHA, full `color`)
116	      - FADE_START < t <= FADE_FULL: eased ramp (FADE_GAMMA) toward darkest
117	                                      (alpha -> 1.0, color -> color*FADE_BOTTOM_DARK)
118	    With FADE_FULL = 1.0 the ramp runs to the bottom edge, so there is no flat dark
119	    band — the bottom half is a continuous gradient."""
120	    bottom = tuple(int(c * FADE_BOTTOM_DARK) for c in color)
121	    color_col = Image.new("RGB", (1, h))
122	    alpha_col = Image.new("L", (1, h))
123	    cp = color_col.load()
124	    ap = alpha_col.load()
125	    span = max(1e-6, FADE_FULL - FADE_START)
126	    for y in range(h):
127	        t = y / (h - 1) if h > 1 else 0.0
128	        s = (t - FADE_START) / span          # 0 at FADE_START, 1 at FADE_FULL
129	        s = 0.0 if s < 0.0 else (1.0 if s > 1.0 else s)
130	        s = s ** FADE_GAMMA
131	        cp[0, y] = (int(color[0] * (1.0 - s) + bottom[0] * s),
132	                    int(color[1] * (1.0 - s) + bottom[1] * s),
133	                    int(color[2] * (1.0 - s) + bottom[2] * s))
134	        a = FADE_TOP_ALPHA + (1.0 - FADE_TOP_ALPHA) * s
135	        ap[0, y] = max(0, min(255, int(a * 255)))
136	    return color_col.resize((w, h)), alpha_col.resize((w, h))
137	
138	
139	def make_large(img, color):
140	    """Scale to 508 wide, center-crop the middle 508x208 band, bake the
141	    difficulty-color wash that darkens toward the bottom. Returns an RGB image."""
142	    ratio = LARGE_W / img.width
143	    scaled = img.resize((LARGE_W, max(LARGE_H, int(round(img.height * ratio)))),
144	                        Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
145	    top = (scaled.height - LARGE_H) // 2
146	    strip = scaled.crop((0, top, LARGE_W, top + LARGE_H))
147	
148	    overlay, alpha = build_fade(LARGE_W, LARGE_H, color)
149	    return Image.composite(overlay, strip, alpha)
150	
151	
152	def make_small(img):
153	    """Scale to fit a 144x144 box, pillarbox/letterbox on black. Returns RGB."""
154	    scale = min(SMALL_SIZE / img.width, SMALL_SIZE / img.height)
155	    new_w = int(img.width * scale)
156	    new_h = int(img.height * scale)
157	    scaled = img.resize((new_w, new_h), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
158	    canvas = Image.new("RGB", (SMALL_SIZE, SMALL_SIZE), (0, 0, 0))
159	    canvas.paste(scaled, ((SMALL_SIZE - new_w) // 2, (SMALL_SIZE - new_h) // 2))
160	    return canvas
161	
162	
163	def clear_covers(d):
164	    """Remove existing cover files (any image extension) from a tier dir, so a
165	    re-run leaves no stale files behind (e.g. old .jpg larges)."""
166	    for f in d.iterdir():
167	        if f.is_file() and f.suffix.lower() in (".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png"):
168	            f.unlink()
169	
170	
171	def process_cover_art(src_dir, out_base, catalog_path):
172	    """Process all JPGs in src_dir into the marvin art tree."""
173	    src_path = Path(src_dir)
174	
175	    out_large = Path(out_base) / "large"
176	    out_small = Path(out_base) / "small"
177	    out_large.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
178	    out_small.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
179	    clear_covers(out_large)
180	    clear_covers(out_small)
181	
182	    difficulty = load_difficulty(catalog_path)
183	
184	    jpg_files = sorted(f for f in src_path.iterdir()
185	                       if f.is_file() and f.suffix.lower() in (".jpg", ".jpeg"))
186	    if not jpg_files:
187	        print(f"No JPG files found in {src_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
188	        return 1
189	
190	    print(f"Processing {len(jpg_files)} cover images -> {out_base}\n")
191	
192	    processed = 0
193	    failed = []
194	
195	    for jpg_path in jpg_files:
196	        try:
197	            m = KEY_RE.match(jpg_path.name)
198	            if not m:
199	                print(f"  WARNING: {jpg_path.name} has no <setlist>_<idx>_ prefix; skipped")
200	                continue
201	            setlist, index = m.group(1), int(m.group(2))
202	            key = (setlist, index)
203	            stem = f"{setlist}-{index:02d}"            # firmware naming
204	            color = difficulty_color(difficulty.get(key))
205	
206	            img = Image.open(jpg_path)
207	            if img.mode in ("RGBA", "LA", "P"):
208	                rgb = Image.new("RGB", img.size, (255, 255, 255))
209	                rgb.paste(img, mask=img.split()[-1] if img.mode == "RGBA" else None)
210	                img = rgb
211	            elif img.mode != "RGB":
212	                img = img.convert("RGB")
213	
214	            # large: PNG strip with baked difficulty fade
215	            make_large(img, color).save(out_large / (stem + ".png"), "PNG")
216	            # small: clean 144x144 JPEG
217	            make_small(img).save(out_small / (stem + ".jpg"), "JPEG", quality=92)
218	
219	            print(f"  {jpg_path.name}: tier {difficulty.get(key) or '-'} "
220	                  f"color {color} -> large/{stem}.png, small/{stem}.jpg")
221	            processed += 1
222	
223	        except Exception as e:
224	            print(f"  ERROR {jpg_path.name}: {e}")
225	            failed.append((jpg_path.name, str(e)))
226	
227	    print(f"\n✓ Processed {processed}/{len(jpg_files)} images")
228	    if failed:
229	        print(f"✗ Failed: {len(failed)}")
230	        for name, error in failed:
231	            print(f"  - {name}: {error}")
232	        return 1
233	
234	    print(f"\nInstalled to:")
235	    print(f"  {out_large}  (song-select, PNG, difficulty fade)")
236	    print(f"  {out_small}  (dashboard, JPEG)")
237	    return 0

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 21:01:50Z)**_

That reframes it well — and yes, **converting on marvin is the right call, not the offline tool.** Here's the reasoning:

The small thumbnail's display target is the **RGB565 base** (dashboard). The current code stores it as RGBA8888 because [art.c:24-27](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/art.c#L24-L27) assumes "the display layer is RGBA8888" — but that's only true for the **large** tier (its own OVR2 layer). For the small tier that assumption is wrong; the final pixels are RGB565 no matter what the slot holds.

So decoding the small JPEG straight into an **RGB565 slot** is strictly better:

- **Display is identical** — the base is 565 either way, so you lose nothing you saw in the comparison.
- **Native 565→565 copy blit** instead of RGBA8888→565. That sidesteps the `SRC_OVER` alpha-blend path *and* the `alpha=0xFF` fix-up hack ([art.c:266](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/art.c#L266)) — a decode that leaves alpha=0 renders fully transparent, which is a real candidate for "album art not working." RGB565 has no alpha channel, so it's always opaque.
- **Halves the small pool RAM**: `GP_N_SONGS × 144×144×4` → `×2` (~2.8 MB saved).
- **No offline change, no asset regen** — the small covers stay JPEG on the card. So scrap the "update process_gh3_cover_art + regenerate" plan.

The offline-raw-565 alternative (bake a raw 565 blob, skip runtime decode) would only buy a little boot time on the small tier and costs a new asset format + loader + tool change + regen — not worth it.

**Concrete change, all in [art.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/art.c):** make the tier BPP/color-mode per-tier instead of the shared `ART_BPP=4` — small → `RGB_565` (2 B/px), large → `RGBA_8888` (4 B/px). Thread the color mode into the decode path (`decode_one` currently hardcodes `LE_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888`), and skip the alpha fix-up for the 565 tier. `Art_Small` then returns an RGB565 `leImage`; the dashboard `setImage` becomes a plain copy. Large tier and song-select are untouched.

Want me to make that change?

88	/* "main"/"bonus" (any case) -> GP_SETLIST_*, or -1. */
89	static int setlist_id(const char *s, size_t n)
90	{
91	    if (ieq(s, n, "main"))  { return GP_SETLIST_MAIN; }
92	    if (ieq(s, n, "bonus")) { return GP_SETLIST_BONUS; }
93	    return -1;
94	}
95	
96	/* Parse "<setlist>-<NN>.<ext>" -> setlist, index, image format. */
97	static bool parse_name(const char *fname, uint8_t *setlist, uint8_t *index,
98	                       leImageFormat *fmt)
99	{
100	    const char *dash = strchr(fname, '-');
101	    const char *dot  = strrchr(fname, '.');
102	    if (dash == NULL || dot == NULL || dot < dash) { return false; }
103	
104	    int sl = setlist_id(fname, (size_t)(dash - fname));
105	    if (sl < 0) { return false; }
106	
107	    const char *ext = dot + 1;
108	    if (ext_is(ext, "png"))                            { *fmt = LE_IMAGE_FORMAT_PNG; }
109	    else if (ext_is(ext, "jpg") || ext_is(ext, "jpeg")) { *fmt = LE_IMAGE_FORMAT_JPEG; }
110	    else { return false; }
111	
112	    *setlist = (uint8_t)sl;
113	    *index   = (uint8_t)atoi(dash + 1);
114	    return true;
115	}
116	
117	/* True image dimensions from the compressed header (the destination raster is
118	 * sized from these, so they must be exact). */
119	static bool jpeg_dims(const uint8_t *b, uint32_t n, uint16_t *w, uint16_t *h)
120	{
121	    if (n < 4u || b[0] != 0xFFu || b[1] != 0xD8u) { return false; }
122	
123	    uint32_t i = 2u;
124	    while (i + 1u < n)
125	    {
126	        if (b[i] != 0xFFu) { i++; continue; }
127	
128	        uint8_t m = b[i + 1u];
129	        i += 2u;
130	
131	        /* Standalone markers (no length field). */
132	        if (m == 0xD8u || m == 0xD9u || (m >= 0xD0u && m <= 0xD7u) || m == 0x01u) { continue; }
133	        if (i + 1u >= n) { break; }
134	
135	        uint16_t seg = (uint16_t)((b[i] << 8) | b[i + 1u]);
136	
137	        /* SOF markers carry frame dimensions; exclude DHT(C4)/JPG(C8)/DAC(CC). */
138	        if (m >= 0xC0u && m <= 0xCFu && m != 0xC4u && m != 0xC8u && m != 0xCCu)
139	        {
140	            if (i + 7u > n) { break; }
141	            *h = (uint16_t)((b[i + 3u] << 8) | b[i + 4u]);
142	            *w = (uint16_t)((b[i + 5u] << 8) | b[i + 6u]);
143	            return true;
144	        }
145	
146	        i += seg;   /* length includes its own 2 bytes */
147	    }
148	    return false;
149	}
150	
151	static bool png_dims(const uint8_t *b, uint32_t n, uint16_t *w, uint16_t *h)
152	{
153	    if (n < 24u) { return false; }
154	    if (b[0] != 0x89u || b[1] != 0x50u || b[2] != 0x4Eu || b[3] != 0x47u) { return false; }
155	
156	    /* IHDR width/height are 4-byte big-endian at offsets 16 and 20; our sizes fit
157	     * 16 bits, so take the low two bytes of each. */
158	    *w = (uint16_t)((b[18] << 8) | b[19]);
159	    *h = (uint16_t)((b[22] << 8) | b[23]);
160	    return true;
161	}
162	
163	/* ---- decode ------------------------------------------------------------- */
164	
165	/* DIAGNOSTIC: fill slots with a known RGBA8888 pattern instead of decoding from
166	 * the card, to isolate the display path (GFX2D blit -> canvas -> XLCDC) from the
167	 * PNG/JPEG decode. Set to 0 for real artwork. Pattern: R ramps left->right, G ramps
168	 * top->bottom, B=0x40, opaque, with a 1px white border. Correct display = smooth 2D
169	 * gradient framed edge-to-edge; stride bugs shear the R ramp / break the border;
170	 * a height truncation stops the G ramp early and drops the bottom border; a
171	 * byte-order bug swaps which axis is red vs green/blue. */
172	#define ART_TEST_PATTERN 0
173	
174	#if ART_TEST_PATTERN
175	static void fill_test_pattern(uint8_t *slot, uint16_t w, uint16_t h)
176	{
177	    uint32_t *px = (uint32_t *)(void *)slot;
178	    for (uint16_t y = 0u; y < h; y++)
179	    {
180	        for (uint16_t x = 0u; x < w; x++)
181	        {
182	            uint8_t r = (uint8_t)((uint32_t)x * 255u / (w - 1u));
183	            uint8_t g = (uint8_t)((uint32_t)y * 255u / (h - 1u));
184	            uint32_t c = ((uint32_t)r << 24) | ((uint32_t)g << 16) | (0x40u << 8) | 0xFFu;
185	            if (x == 0u || y == 0u || x == (w - 1u) || y == (h - 1u)) { c = 0xFFFFFFFFu; }
186	            px[(uint32_t)y * w + x] = c;
187	        }
188	    }
189	}
190	#endif
191	
192	/* Read one cover file into scratch, verify it matches the tier slot dimensions,
193	 * and decode it into the slot as RGBA8888 via the Legato JPEG/PNG decoder. Fills
194	 * *out_img (RAW, RGBA8888, pointing at slot_px) on success. */
195	static bool decode_one(const char *path, leImageFormat fmt,
196	                       uint8_t *slot_px, uint16_t w_exp, uint16_t h_exp,
197	                       leImage *out_img)
198	{
199	#if ART_TEST_PATTERN
200	    (void)path; (void)fmt;
201	    fill_test_pattern(slot_px, w_exp, h_exp);
202	    (void)leImage_Create(out_img, w_exp, h_exp, LE_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, slot_px,
203	                         LE_STREAM_LOCATION_ID_INTERNAL);
204	    out_img->flags |= LE_IMAGE_DIRECT_BLIT;
205	    dcache_CleanByAddr(slot_px, (int32_t)((uint32_t)w_exp * h_exp * ART_BPP));
206	    return true;
207	#else
208	    SYS_FS_HANDLE h = SYS_FS_FileOpen(path, SYS_FS_FILE_OPEN_READ);
209	    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)
210	    {
211	        LOG_WARN("ART: open '%s' failed (fs err %d)\r\n", path, (int)SYS_FS_Error());
212	        return false;
213	    }
214	
215	    int32_t size = SYS_FS_FileSize(h);
216	    if (size <= 0 || (uint32_t)size > ART_SCRATCH_BYTES)
217	    {
218	        LOG_WARN("ART: '%s' size %ld out of range\r\n", path, (long)size);
219	        (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
220	        return false;
221	    }
222	    size_t got = SYS_FS_FileRead(h, s_scratch, (size_t)size);
223	    (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
224	    if (got != (size_t)size) { LOG_WARN("ART: '%s' short read\r\n", path); return false; }
225	
226	    uint16_t iw = 0u, ih = 0u;
227	    bool ok = (fmt == LE_IMAGE_FORMAT_PNG)
228	                  ? png_dims(s_scratch, (uint32_t)size, &iw, &ih)
229	                  : jpeg_dims(s_scratch, (uint32_t)size, &iw, &ih);
230	    if (!ok) { LOG_WARN("ART: '%s' header dims unreadable\r\n", path); return false; }
231	    if (iw != w_exp || ih != h_exp)
232	    {
233	        LOG_WARN("ART: '%s' is %ux%u, expected %ux%u\r\n",
234	                 path, (unsigned)iw, (unsigned)ih, (unsigned)w_exp, (unsigned)h_exp);
235	        return false;
236	    }
237	
238	    /* Source: compressed bytes in scratch, described as a JPEG/PNG image.
239	     * leImage_Create stamps header.size with the *decoded* size; the PNG decoder
240	     * passes header.size to lodepng as the *compressed* input length, so override
241	     * it with the real file size (harmless for the marker-driven JPEG path). */
242	    leImage src;
243	    (void)leImage_Create(&src, iw, ih, LE_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888, s_scratch,
244	                         LE_STREAM_LOCATION_ID_INTERNAL);
245	    src.format       = fmt;
246	    src.header.size  = (uint32_t)size;
247	
248	    /* Destination: the fixed slot, as a RAW RGBA8888 image. LE_IMAGE_DIRECT_BLIT
249	     * routes the on-paint draw through the RAW decoder's _directBlit (a per-row
250	     * memcpy) instead of the per-pixel software blit: the 2D engine can't blit an
251	     * RGBA8888 source (it's an "alpha mode" → SRC_OVER blend, which the copy-only
252	     * GFX2D path declines), so without this every selection re-blits the cover
253	     * pixel-by-pixel (visible hesitation). The slot mode matches the RGBA8888 layer,
254	     * which _directBlit requires, and the cover is opaque so an overwrite is correct. */
255	    (void)leImage_Create(out_img, iw, ih, LE_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, slot_px,
256	                         LE_STREAM_LOCATION_ID_INTERNAL);
257	    out_img->flags |= LE_IMAGE_DIRECT_BLIT;
258	
259	    leRect full = { 0, 0, (int32_t)iw, (int32_t)ih };
260	    /* Decode straight into the slot. leImage_Render's return is unreliable
261	     * (always LE_FAILURE even on success), so we trust the validated dims +
262	     * known format, mirroring how leProcessImage drives the decoder. */
263	    (void)leImage_Render(&src, &full, 0, 0, LE_TRUE, LE_TRUE, out_img);
264	
265	    /* Force opaque alpha. The covers are fully opaque (the fade is baked into RGB),
266	     * but a JPEG/PNG-without-alpha decode into RGBA8888 can leave the alpha byte 0,
267	     * which renders the image fully transparent. RGBA_8888 packs 0xRRGGBBAA, so
268	     * alpha is the low byte. */
269	    uint32_t *px  = (uint32_t *)(void *)slot_px;
270	    size_t    npx = (size_t)iw * ih;
271	    for (size_t i = 0; i < npx; i++) { px[i] |= 0x000000FFu; }
272	
273	    /* The decode wrote the slot via the CPU (write-back cache); flush it to DDR.
274	     * With LE_IMAGE_DIRECT_BLIT the on-paint draw is a CPU memcpy (slot read via
275	     * CPU, coherent), so this isn't strictly needed — but it's a cheap one-time
276	     * clean of a write-once buffer and keeps DDR correct for any 2D-engine fallback
277	     * path (leGPU_BlitBuffer DMA-reads the slot). 32-byte aligned, exact-multiple
278	     * size → clean line boundaries, no neighbor interference. */
279	    dcache_CleanByAddr(slot_px, (int32_t)((uint32_t)iw * ih * ART_BPP));
280	    return true;
281	#endif /* ART_TEST_PATTERN */
282	}
283	
284	/* Scan scratch (reused across the two sequential load_tier calls): the dir walk
285	 * collects entries here, then the dir is closed before any file is opened. */
286	typedef struct { uint8_t setlist; uint8_t index; leImageFormat fmt; } art_scan_t;
287	static art_scan_t s_scan[GP_N_SONGS];
288	
289	/* Load one tier subdir's covers into its pool. Two phases because FatFs is built
290	 * with FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1 — only one open object at a time — so we must close the
291	 * directory handle before opening any file (otherwise every SYS_FS_FileOpen
292	 * returns FR_TOO_MANY_OPEN_FILES). Returns the number decoded. */
293	static int load_tier(const char *subdir, uint8_t *pool, size_t slot_bytes,
294	                     uint16_t w, uint16_t h, leImage *imgs, art_key_t *keys)
295	{
296	    char dirpath[ART_PATH_MAX];
297	    (void)snprintf(dirpath, sizeof dirpath, "%s/%s/%s",
298	                   Storage_MountPoint(), ART_DIR_REL, subdir);
299	
300	    /* Phase 1 — collect "<setlist>-<NN>.<ext>" entries, then close the dir. */
301	    SYS_FS_HANDLE dh = SYS_FS_DirOpen(dirpath);
302	    if (dh == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)
303	    {
304	        LOG_WARN("ART: opendir '%s' failed (fs err %d)\r\n", dirpath, (int)SYS_FS_Error());
305	        return 0;
306	    }
307	
308	    int n = 0, seen = 0;
309	    SYS_FS_FSTAT st;
310	    while (n < GP_N_SONGS)
311	    {
312	        memset(&st, 0, sizeof st);
313	        st.lfname = NULL;
314	        st.lfsize = 0u;
315	
316	        if (SYS_FS_DirRead(dh, &st) != SYS_FS_RES_SUCCESS) { break; }
317	        if (st.fname[0] == '\0') { break; }                 /* end of directory */
318	        if ((st.fattrib & SYS_FS_ATTR_DIR) != 0u) { continue; }
319	        if (st.fname[0] == '.') { continue; }               /* skip ._ AppleDouble & dotfiles */
320	
321	        seen++;
322	        if (parse_name(st.fname, &s_scan[n].setlist, &s_scan[n].index, &s_scan[n].fmt))
323	        {
324	            n++;
325	        }
326	    }
327	    (void)SYS_FS_DirClose(dh);
328	
329	    /* Phase 2 — decode each collected cover (dir closed → one file open at a time).
330	     * Reconstruct the path from the key so we never touch a stray filename. */
331	    int count = 0;
332	    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
333	    {
334	        const char *setname = (s_scan[i].setlist == GP_SETLIST_BONUS) ? "bonus" : "main";
335	        const char *ext     = (s_scan[i].fmt == LE_IMAGE_FORMAT_PNG) ? "png" : "jpg";
336	        char filepath[ART_PATH_MAX];
337	        (void)snprintf(filepath, sizeof filepath, "%s/%s-%02u.%s",
338	                       dirpath, setname, (unsigned)s_scan[i].index, ext);
339	
340	        uint8_t *slot = pool + (size_t)count * slot_bytes;
341	        if (decode_one(filepath, s_scan[i].fmt, slot, w, h, &imgs[count]))
342	        {
343	            keys[count].setlist = s_scan[i].setlist;
344	            keys[count].index   = s_scan[i].index;
345	            keys[count].valid   = true;
346	            count++;
347	        }
348	    }
349	
350	    LOG_INFO("ART: %s: %d file(s) seen, %d loaded\r\n", subdir, seen, count);
351	    return count;
352	}
353	
354	/* ---- public ------------------------------------------------------------- */
355	
356	void Art_Initialize(void)
357	{
358	    s_small_n = 0;
359	    s_large_n = 0;
360	    s_loaded  = false;
361	}
362	
363	int Art_LoadAll(void)
364	{
365	    if (s_loaded) { return s_small_n + s_large_n; }
366	    s_loaded = true;   /* one attempt; lookups won't trigger a re-load */
367	
368	    if (!Storage_Mount()) { return 0; }
369	
370	    s_small_n = load_tier("small", (uint8_t *)s_small_px, ART_SMALL_SLOT,
371	                          ART_SMALL_W, ART_SMALL_H, s_small_img, s_small_key);
372	    s_large_n = load_tier("large", (uint8_t *)s_large_px, ART_LARGE_SLOT,
373	                          ART_LARGE_W, ART_LARGE_H, s_large_img, s_large_key);
374	
375	    LOG_INFO("ART: loaded %d small, %d large\r\n", s_small_n, s_large_n);
376	    return s_small_n + s_large_n;
377	}
378	
379	bool Art_IsLoaded(void) { return s_loaded; }
380	int  Art_CountSmall(void) { return s_small_n; }
381	int  Art_CountLarge(void) { return s_large_n; }
382	
383	static const leImage *lookup(const art_key_t *keys, const leImage *imgs, int n,
384	                             uint8_t setlist, uint8_t index)
385	{
386	    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
387	    {
388	        if (keys[i].valid && keys[i].setlist == setlist && keys[i].index == index)
389	        {
390	            return &imgs[i];
391	        }
392	    }
393	    return NULL;
394	}
395	
396	const leImage *Art_Small(uint8_t setlist, uint8_t index)
397	{
398	    return lookup(s_small_key, s_small_img, s_small_n, setlist, index);
399	}
400	
401	const leImage *Art_Large(uint8_t setlist, uint8_t index)
402	{
403	    return lookup(s_large_key, s_large_img, s_large_n, setlist, index);
404	}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 21:21:23Z)**_

Done. The small tier now decodes into its display layer's native format.

## What changed — [art.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/art.c)

The slot format is now **per-tier**, matching the hardware layer each is shown on:

- **small → RGB565** (2 B/px) — the dashboard thumbnail lives on the RGB565 BASE
- **large → RGBA8888** (4 B/px) — the song-select strip has its own full-color OVR2 layer (unchanged)

Threaded a `leColorMode` through `load_tier` → `decode_one`; the Legato JPEG decoder renders straight into the 565 slot. Three consequences, all good:

1. **Native 565→565 copy** via the standard image-draw path (2D engine), which correctly positions/clips the thumbnail inside the full-screen dashboard canvas. `LE_IMAGE_DIRECT_BLIT` is now applied **only to the large tier** (its alpha-mode source is what the 2D engine declines) — the small tier doesn't need it, avoiding the risk that a raw per-row memcpy mishandles sub-region placement.
2. **Alpha fix-up skipped for 565** — no alpha channel, so the "decode leaves alpha=0 → fully transparent" hazard (a real candidate for "art not showing") can't happen for the thumbnail anymore.
3. **~2.5 MB freed** in `.region_ram` (64 songs × 144², 4→2 B/px).

No offline-tool change, **no asset regen** — the small covers stay JPEG on the card. Compiles clean with XC32 v5.10; journal updated. Pending your hardware test — this is also the change most likely to fix the "album art not working" symptom, so worth a close look at the dashboard thumbnail on boot.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 21:37:44Z)**_

Found it — line 955: the JPEG decoder only blits each block if it **intersects `pJpegDecoder->clipRect`**, which `_render` reads from `leRenderer_GetClipRect` (line 336). `Art_LoadAll` calls `leImage_Render` at boot **outside any Legato paint pass**, so that clip rect is stale/empty → no blocks are written → the slot stays uninitialized `.region_ram` = **noise**. This is independent of 565 vs 8888 — it would break both tiers, matching your original "album art not working."

Let me confirm how the renderer clip rect is set, to fix the decode.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 21:46:48Z)**_

Root cause **confirmed and it's format-specific**:

- **PNG `_render`** (large tier) → `lePixelBufferCopy(dst, …)` — a direct color-converting buffer copy, **no clip gating**. Works at boot.
- **JPEG `_render`** (small tier) → blits block-by-block, each gated by the stale renderer clip rect. At boot it decodes to noise.

Small covers are `.jpg`, large are `.png` — that's exactly why "mostly working but for album art." It's not the 565 change; JPEG offscreen-decode was always broken here.

Two clean fixes. Let me check how invasive the no-regen option is before recommending.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 21:55:09Z)**_

I checked the "internal mechanism" angle — good instinct, but it confirms PNG. The supported offscreen-decode entry point is `leProcessImage` ([legato_image.c:418](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/image/legato_image.c#L418)) — what Legato/MGS uses to pre-decode a stream image into a RAM buffer. It calls the **identical** `leImage_Render` with no clip setup, so it hits the same JPEG block-clip gating. And the public renderer API has no clip *setter* (only `GetClipRect`). MGS's "pre-render assets" is a **build-time** decode that bakes assets to RAW in flash — not a runtime JPEG path. So there's no supported runtime offscreen JPEG decode that dodges this; PNG's `lePixelBufferCopy` path is the clip-independent one. Your call is right.

Implementing: small tier → PNG in the offline tool, then regenerate.

292:Built the cover-art cache that spec §4.8.7 called for; resolves Q13. New `game/art.{c,h}`: two fixed-size **RGBA8888** tiers in cached DDR (`.region_ram`) — small 144×144 (5.3 MB), large 508×208 (27 MB) — plus a 512 KB shared decode scratch (~33 MB total). (Originally RGB888 ~23 MB; switched to RGBA8888 so the cover source matches the RGBA8888 display layer and is 2D-engine-blittable — see the full-color entry below.) `Art_LoadAll()` runs in `ui_boot_task` **before** `init_screens()` (Legato decoders are up from SYS_Initialize; it mounts storage itself) so the cache is populated when `ScreenSongSelect_Setup` → `song_detail_show(0)` paints the initial selection's cover; the ~1–3 s of JPEG/PNG decode is hidden behind the splash. It walks `art/{small,large}/` via `SYS_FS_DirOpen`/`DirRead` in **two phases** — collect the `<setlist>-<NN>.<ext>` entries, **close the dir**, then open+decode each (FatFs here is `FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1`, so a dir handle and a file handle can't be open at once; holding the dir open made every `SYS_FS_FileOpen` return `FR_TOO_MANY_OPEN_FILES`=18 — the bug that made the first cut load 0/0 despite the files being present). Phase 2 reconstructs each path from the `(setlist,index,fmt)` key, which also sidesteps macOS `._` AppleDouble cruft on the card. It reads each file into scratch, reads true dims from the JPEG `SOF`/PNG `IHDR` header (the destination raster is sized from these), requires an exact tier-dimension match, then decodes into the slot with `leImage_Render` — the JPEG/PNG decoder `render` path writes RGB888 straight into the slot via `lePixelBufferSet`+`leColorConvert`, with no dependence on the screen clip rect or an active paint frame (verified by reading the decoder). Each slot is wrapped as a RAW RGB888 `leImage`; `Art_Large/Small(setlist,index)` is a linear scan → `leImage*` or NULL. Missing/oversize/wrong-size/corrupt → empty slot → UI blank, never a boot failure.
296:Offline (`tools/gh3-cover-art/`): `process_gh3_cover_art.py` reworked — large output is now a center-cropped 508×208 strip with a difficulty-colored top/bottom fade baked in, read per song from `songs.csv` (`"1".."8"` → an 8-tier palette green→red with blue/purple accents via `TIER_COLORS`, `"bonus"`/unknown → gray), saved as PNG (lossless gradient). Small stays 144×144 letterboxed JPEG. `install_art.py` installs large as `<setlist>-NN.png`. Fade tunables (`FADE_TOP_ALPHA`/`FADE_BOTTOM_DARK`/`FADE_GAMMA`) at the top of the script.
300:Status / bring-up bugs found & fixed (all on hardware): (1) **FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1** — the dir handle + a file handle can't both be open, so the first cut logged `0 small, 0 large` (`FR_TOO_MANY_OPEN_FILES`=18); fixed by the two-phase walk above. (2) **`png_dims` read the wrong IHDR bytes** (high 2 of the 4-byte width/height, always 0) → every large PNG parsed 0×0; fixed to read the low two bytes. (3) **`leImage_Create` stamps `header.size` with the *decoded* size, but the PNG decoder passes it to lodepng as the *compressed* input length** → lodepng read past the file into stale scratch → silent decode failure (black); fixed by setting `src.header.size = compressed file size`. (4) **GFX2D cache coherency** — the decode writes the slot via the CPU (write-back), but Legato draws the image with `leGPU_BlitBuffer` (2D engine DMA-reads DDR), so it saw stale/zero DDR → black; fixed with a one-time `dcache_CleanByAddr(slot)` after decode (sufficient because the slot is write-once, unlike the per-frame scratch that had to go non-cached in 2026-06-24). A per-tier diagnostic logs files-seen/loaded + the first cover's center pixel (kept through bring-up). With these, both tiers decode to valid pixels and the strip renders.
302:**Full-color via a dedicated layer-screen (done; 2026-06-30).** Song-select stays **RGB565** (DDR bandwidth); the large art is its **own MGS layer-screen** — Marvin **layer 3, RGBA8888**, a 508×208 canvas composited on **OVR2 above the dialog on OVR1**, so only the art rect pays 32bpp (~0.42 MB). `LE_LAYER_COUNT` is now 4. **RGBA8888, not RGB888:** the 2D engine has **no RGB888 support** (`gfx2dFormats[GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888] = -1`; only `RGB_565`→`GFX2D_RGB16` and `RGBA_8888`→`GFX2D_ARGB32`), so a 24bpp canvas can't be GFX2D-blitted scratch→canvas and renders as static garbage (confirmed on hardware: OVR2 showed a fixed white-ish pattern). MGS authored the layer as `RGB_888`; `ui_manager` overrides it to `LE_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888` right after `screenShow_Marvin` (set the layer-screen to RGBA8888 in MGS to make the override redundant). The cover **cache** (`game/art.c`) is also **RGBA8888** (4 B/px) so the source matches the layer and the 2D engine can blit it natively (RGB888 is unblittable as *source* too — `gfx2dFormats[RGB_888] = -1`). Covers are opaque (fade baked into RGB), so `decode_one` forces the alpha byte to 0xFF after `leImage_Render` (a JPEG/PNG-without-alpha decode into RGBA8888 can leave alpha 0 → fully transparent → invisible). Cache size rose to ~33 MB cached DDR (large 27 MB + small 5.3 MB + 0.5 MB scratch) — fine in the 224 MB region. MGS hosts the cover image **plus the TIER/title/artist labels** on this layer (they overlay the art at full color); album/year/genre/duration stay on the RGB565 dialog. New firmware: `ui/screens/album_art/screen_album_art.{c,h}` (canvas `CANVAS_ALBUM_ART`=3, `GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888` 4 B/px buffer in `.region_nocache`, cleared to opaque black since NOLOAD, window at screen (433,160)); `ui_manager` reveal now binds **song-select→OVR1**, **album-art→OVR2** (`XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888`), and **no longer binds nav at boot** — `navigation_open()` grabs OVR1 only while shown (nav and the dialog share OVR1, mutually exclusive). Good memory, and the git history sharpens the picture. Here's the honest reconciliation:

**Large was never actually shipped as JPEG.** `git log` shows the large tier has only ever been `*.png` on the card (first art commit onward). The journal's rationale — *"PNG for large because the smooth baked gradient bands under JPEG"* — was the **design reason** for choosing PNG, but large went straight to PNG; there was no working jpg-large era.

**And here's the key correction.** That same journal entry claims the decoder writes into the slot *"with no dependence on the screen clip rect or an active paint frame (verified by reading the decoder)"* — and the bring-up log lists all its fixes on **PNG** covers (png_dims, lodepng header.size, GFX2D cache). That "no clip dependence" claim is **true for PNG, false for JPEG.** The author validated the large/PNG path on hardware and assumed JPEG's offscreen `_render` behaved the same. It doesn't — line 955 gates every JPEG block on the renderer clip rect. The small/JPEG tier was "dashboard pending," never hardware-verified, so the wrong assumption never surfaced until now.

So the two things that made large "just work" — chosen for the gradient **and** landing on PNG's clip-independent `lePixelBufferCopy` path — are why it renders. Small stayed JPEG and hits the clip gate → noise.

**Why PNG-for-small is safe, not a shot in the dark:**
- It's the *same* decode path already hardware-validated on 64 large covers.
- Small PNG → `lePixelBufferCopy` color-converts into the 565 slot; no clip dependency.
- Heap headroom is fine: `LE_VARIABLEHEAP_SIZE` is 2 MB (raised for large's ~740 KB PNG peak); a 144×144 PNG peaks ~166 KB.

Nothing missed on the JPEG side — the clip gate is real and there's no supported runtime hook to set the clip for an offscreen JPEG decode. PNG it is.

Want me to go ahead and run the regeneration now? (It rewrites `art/small/*.jpg` → `*.png` and leaves the rest untouched.)

9	**2026-07-01 — Small album-art tier → RGB565 (matches its display layer).** The dashboard now-playing thumbnail is shown on the **RGB565 BASE** layer, so decoding the small tier into RGBA8888 was pointless — the final pixels are 565 regardless. A 565-vs-888 comparison on the real 144×144 covers confirmed the depth is visually indistinguishable (banding only shows on synthetic smooth gradients, which photographic covers aren't; the *large* strip's baked difficulty fade is the only gradient asset and keeps its own RGBA8888 OVR2 layer). `game/art.c` now decodes each tier into its **layer-matching** mode: **small = RGB565 (2 B/px)**, large = RGBA8888 (4 B/px), threaded through `load_tier`/`decode_one` as a `leColorMode`. Wins: (1) native 565→565 copy blit for the thumbnail via the standard draw path (2D engine), which correctly positions/clips within the full-screen dashboard canvas — **no `LE_IMAGE_DIRECT_BLIT`** for small (kept for large, whose alpha-mode source the 2D engine declines); (2) the RGBA8888 `alpha |= 0xFF` opaque-fixup is skipped for 565 (no alpha channel — and a decode leaving alpha=0 would have rendered the thumbnail fully transparent, a real "art not showing" hazard now gone); (3) small pool RAM halves, ~5.1 MB → ~2.5 MB in `.region_ram` (64 songs). No offline-tool change and **no asset regen** — small covers stay JPEG on the card. Builds clean (XC32 v5.10). **Pending hardware test.**
10	
11	**2026-07-01 — Selection seam: song-select SELECT → dashboard SONG card (gameplay-engine groundwork).** First step toward the gameplay engine: a committed-selection state that both the dashboard and the future engine read. New `game/selection.{c,h}` holds `{setlist, index, difficulty, mode}` keyed on the recognizer's stable `(setlist,index)` (matches `Art_*`/`Catalog_*`); pure static state, single observer, `valid=false` until the first `Selection_Set` (static zero-init, no init-call/`app.c` wiring). **SELECT commits, X cancels** — `screen_song_select.c` now retains the highlighted list index (`s_sel_index`), and SELECT calls `songsel_commit()` → `Selection_Set(...)`; the X button just closes (no commit). Setup seeds a boot default by committing the first-song selection once (after `song_detail_show(0)`), so the card isn't a figma placeholder at boot. `screen_dashboard.c` registers a `Selection` observer (`dash_selection_changed`) that mirrors the selection onto the MGS SONG-card widgets via the same per-label `leFixedString` mechanism the dialog uses: `AlbumArt`←`Art_Small`, `SongTitle/Artist/Genre`, `SongAlbum`=`"album - year"` (card has no separate year label), `SongDuration`, `SongTier` (stars+color), `GAMEPLAY_GameMode` (`1P ROBOT`/`1P HUMAN`/`2P R vs H`, ASCII — no `•` in the DejaVu mono subset), and the `GAMEPLAY_Difficulty` pill (text + fill recolored via `SCHEME_BUTTON_EASY/MEDIUM/HARD/EXPERT`). Naming rule confirmed: MGS **dynamic** labels end camelCase (`_SongTitle`, `_GameMode`), **fixed** labels ALL-CAPS (`_GENRE`, `_MODE`) and are left alone. Shared tier/duration formatting factored out of `screen_song_select.c` into new `ui/song_detail.{c,h}` (`SongDetail_Tier`/`TierText`/`TierScheme`/`Duration`), so the dialog and dashboard use one palette. `Status` label left as MGS "READY" (gameplay-driven later). Observer ordering relies on `ui_manager` calling `ScreenDashboard_Setup` (registers observer) before `ScreenSongSelect_Setup` (seeds default). Builds clean (XC32 v5.10, all four sources); **pending hardware test.**
12	
13	**2026-07-01 — Dashboard redesign: dedicated SELECT SONG button; top-bar tap retired.** MGS regenerated the Marvin screen with a reworked dashboard: the old `PANEL_BASE_TOP`/`PANEL_BASE_BOTTOM`/`PANEL_SYSTEM_*`/`PANEL_ROBOT_CONTROLS` are gone, replaced by `PANEL_DASHBOARD_TOP`/`_BOTTOM` (+ `_TOP_LEFT`/`_TOP_RIGHT`), and the guitar strum buttons were dropped. Three code effects: (1) **Song select** now opens from a real `BUTTON_DASHBOARD_GAMEPLAY_SELECT_SONG` button (released-callback → `UiManager_OpenSongSelect`), replacing the old header-panel vtable-tap hack in `screen_dashboard.c`. (2) `screen_video.c`'s fullscreen input-gate retargeted from `BASE_TOP/BASE_BOTTOM` to `DASHBOARD_TOP/DASHBOARD_BOTTOM`. (3) This regen dropped **all** MGS auto-event wiring, so the hamburger (renamed `BUTTON_NAV_HAMBURGER`, now under `DASHBOARD_TOP_LEFT`) is wired explicitly in `ScreenNavigation_Setup` via `setPressedEventCallback`; the orphaned `event_Marvin_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION_OnPressed` was removed. The guitar strum glue in `manual_input.c` is kept as-is (orphaned but preserved) — the `ManualControl` actuator logic stays even though the UI no longer drives it, so the strum buttons can be reattached later. **Pending hardware test / build.**
14	
15	**2026-07-01 — HEO video levels expansion (gamma CLUT).** The captured source is mildly range-compressed vs the panel's full 0..255 — corpus measurement (active area, borders excluded): black cluster ~5 (dead border pedestal ~13, cropped out), white ceiling ~233, nothing ≥235. The HEO CBHS limited-range black-level block is **YCbCr-only** (datasheet §6.2.6.7 / SAM9X7 DS), so it can't touch our RGB888 HEO input; instead we use the HEO **per-component gamma CLUT** (works on true RGB, `HEOCFG1.GAM`), loaded once with a linear levels-expansion curve (`out = clamp((in−5)·255/228)`, `VIDEO_LEVELS_BLACK=5`, `WHITE=233`). Display-only — the DDR capture is untouched so the detector/gameplay see raw pixels — and free at scanout. Loaded in `UiManager_Initialize` while GAM/CLUTEN are clear (required to write `LCDC_HEOCLUT[256]`); `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode` rewrites `HEOCFG1` with `GAM(0)` on every bind, so `heo_bind` re-asserts `GAM` after it. Fixed curve (no runtime knob for the *values*), but a **`gamma <on|off>` console command** toggles the whole expansion on/off (`UiManager_SetVideoLevels`, gates `GAM` in `heo_bind` + requests a rebind) for A/B eyeballing on the panel. **Code-complete, pending hardware test** — the ~5/233 pedestal/ceiling may differ per Wii/converter, retune `VIDEO_LEVELS_*` if needed. Earlier "blacks already at 0" was wrong — conflated the rare true-0 outliers with the ~5 cluster; corrected here.
